Zou Ji Opening section bracket 〈 (Zheng Weiheng, Ke Xian)〉 Yi Qian Opening section bracket 〈 (Huang Ji)〉 Huang Ze Opening section bracket 〈 (Kong Youliang)〉 Fan Ji, Liao Rang Opening section bracket 〈 (Guo You, Hu Zhonglun, Hua Min, Jia Bin)〉 Zuo Ding Opening section bracket 〈 (Lian Gang)〉 Cao Kai Opening section bracket 〈 (Xu Shida)〉 Liu Wei Opening section bracket 〈 (Shang Chi)〉 Dan Yu Opening section bracket 〈 (Yao Xian, Yang Hao)〉 Zhang Zhao Opening section bracket 〈 (He Yang)〉 Gao Yao Opening section bracket 〈 (Hu Chen)〉
2
鄒緝，字仲熙，吉水人。 洪武中舉明經，授星子教諭。 建文時入為國子助教。 成祖即位，擢翰林侍講。 立東宮，兼左中允，屢署國子監事。 永樂十九年，三殿災，詔求直言，緝上疏曰：
Zou Ji, whose style was Zhongxi, came from Jishui. In the Hongwu era he passed the Classics examination and was made instructor at Xingzi. Under the Jianwen emperor he entered the capital as an assistant instructor at the National University. When the Yongle Emperor came to power, he was promoted to Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting. After the heir apparent was installed, he also held the post of Left Vice-Director of the Household and often served in an acting capacity as Superintendent of the National University. In the nineteenth year of Yongle, fire destroyed the three main halls; the throne called for frank counsel, and Ji submitted a memorial that read:
3
陛下肇建北京，焦勞聖慮，幾二十年。 工大費繁，調度甚廣，冗官蠶食，耗費國儲。 工作之夫，動以百萬，終歲供役，不得躬親田畝以事力作。 猶且征求無藝，至伐桑棗以供薪，剝桑皮以為楮。 加之官吏橫征，日甚一日。 如前歲買辦顏料，本非土產，動科千百。 民相率斂鈔，購之他所。 大青一斤，價至萬六千貫。 及進納，又多留難，往復展轉，當須二萬貫鈔，而不足供一柱之用。 其後既遣官采之產所，而買辦猶未止。 蓋緣工匠多派牟利，而不顧民艱至此。
Your Majesty first raised Beijing as the capital and has borne the cares of state with anxious toil for nearly twenty years. The construction is vast and costly, requisitions reach everywhere, redundant officials nibble away at revenue, and the national treasury is drained. Laborers on the works run into the millions; conscripted for service all year long, they cannot work their own fields with their own hands. On top of that, levies know no limit—mulberry and jujube are cut for fuel, and mulberry bark is stripped to make paper. To this are added the arbitrary exactions of officials, which grow worse by the day. Take the purchase of pigments the year before last: they were not local products, yet levies ran into the hundreds and thousands of households. The people pooled their paper notes and bought the pigments elsewhere. A single pound of azurite cost as much as sixteen thousand strings of cash. When it was delivered, officials obstructed and delayed again and again; after all the back-and-forth, twenty thousand strings might still not buy enough for a single pillar. Later, although officials were sent to collect pigments at the source, commissioned purchases still did not stop. The reason was that craftsmen were widely assigned to line their own pockets without regard for the people's hardship—hence conditions like these.
4
夫京師天下根本。 人民安則京師安，京師安則國本固而天下安。 自營建以來，工匠小人假托威勢，驅迫移徙，號令方施，廬舍已壞。 孤兒寡婦哭泣叫號，倉皇暴露，莫知所適。 遷移甫定，又復驅令他徒，至有三四徙不得息者。 及其既去，而所空之地，經月逾時，工猶未及。 此陛下所不知，而人民疾怨者也。
The capital is the root of the empire. When the people are at peace, the capital is at peace; when the capital is at peace, the foundation of the state is firm and the realm is secure. Since construction began, petty craftsmen have abused their power, forcing people to relocate—the order has barely been issued when their homes are already torn down. Orphans and widows weep and wail, cast out in panic with nowhere to turn. Hardly have they settled when they are driven to move again—some are relocated three or four times without respite. After they have gone, the land they vacated stands idle for months while work has yet to begin. This is what Your Majesty does not know—and what fills the people with bitterness and resentment.
5
貪官汙吏，遍布內外，剝削及於骨髓。 朝廷每遣一人，即是其人養活之計。 虐取苛求，初無限量。 有司承奉，惟恐不及。 間有廉強自守、不事幹媚者，輒肆讒毀，動得罪譴，無以自明。 是以使者所至，有司公行貨賂，剝下媚上，有同交易。 夫小民所積幾何，而內外上下誅求如此。
Greedy, corrupt officials are everywhere, inside and out, stripping the people to the bone. Every envoy the court sends out treats the mission as his own livelihood. Their cruel seizures and harsh demands know no limit. Local officials carry out their wishes, fearful only of falling short. Now and then an official who is upright and refuses to curry favor is slandered without restraint, punished, and left with no way to clear his name. Wherever envoys go, officials openly take bribes, squeezing those below to please those above, as if it were a trade. How much can common people possibly save when extortion from every level runs so deep?
6
今山東、河南、山西、陜西水旱相仍，民至剝樹皮掘草根以食。 老幼流移，顛踣道路，賣妻鬻子以求茍活。 而京師聚集僧道萬餘人，日耗廩米百餘石，此奪民食以養無用也。
Today in Shandong, Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi floods and droughts follow one another, and the people strip tree bark and dig up grass roots for food. Old and young wander the roads, collapsing along the way, selling wives and children merely to stay alive. Yet in the capital more than ten thousand monks and Daoist priests are gathered, consuming over a hundred shi of granary rice each day—this is taking food from the people to feed the useless.
7
至報效軍士，朝廷厚與糧賜。 及使就役，乃驕傲橫恣，閑遊往來。 此皆奸詭之人，懼還原伍，假此規避，非真有報效之心也。
As for soldiers who have volunteered for service, the court grants them generous rations and rewards. Yet when put to work they grow arrogant and overbearing, wandering about at leisure. These are deceitful men who fear returning to their original units and use the arrangement to evade duty—they do not truly wish to serve.
8
朝廷歲令天下織錦、鑄錢，遣內官買馬外蕃，所出常數千萬，而所取曾不能一二。 馬至雖多，類皆駑下。 責民牧養，騷擾殊甚。 及至死傷，輒令賠補。 馬戶貧困，更鬻妻子。 此尤害之大者。
Each year the court orders brocade woven and coin cast throughout the realm and sends palace eunuchs abroad to buy horses; expenditures run to tens of millions, yet what is obtained scarcely amounts to one or two in ten. Although many horses arrive, most are poor and weak. The people are charged with pasturing them, and the harassment is severe. When horses die or are injured, the people are ordered to make compensation. Horse-keeping households are driven to poverty and again sell wives and children. This is among the greatest of harms.
9
漠北降人，賜居室，盛供帳，意欲招其同類也。 不知來者皆懷窺覘，非真遠慕王化，甘去鄉士。 宜求來朝之後，遣歸本國，不必留為後日子孫患。
Surrendered peoples from the northern steppe are given houses and lavish provisions, in the hope of attracting others of their kind. They do not realize that those who come are scouting and probing—not men who truly admire civilization from afar or willingly leave their homelands. After they have paid court, they should be sent home and not kept on to become a trouble for later generations.
10
至宮觀禱祠之事，有國者所當深戒。 古人有言，淫祀無福。 況事無益以害有益，蠹財妄費者乎！ 凡此數事，皆下失民心，上違天意。 怨讟之興，實由於此。
As for palace shrines and prayer sacrifices, rulers ought to take deep warning. The ancients said that improper sacrifices bring no blessing. How much more when useless practices harm what is useful, wasting wealth in vain! All these matters alike cost you the people's hearts below and offend Heaven's intent above. The rise of resentment and complaint truly stems from this.
11
夫奉天殿者，所以朝群臣，發號令，古所謂明堂也。 而災首及焉，非常之變也。 非省躬責己，大布恩澤，改革政化，疏滌天下窮困之人，不能回上天譴怒。 前有監生生員，以單丁告乞侍親，因而獲罪遣戍者，此實有虧治體。 近者大赦，法司執滯常條，當赦者尚復拘系。 並乞重加湔洗，蠲除租賦，一切勿征。 有司百官全其廩祿，拔簡賢才，申行薦舉，官吏貪贓蠹政者，核其罪而罷黜之。 則人心歡悅，和氣可臻，所以保安宗社，為國家千萬年無窮之基，莫有大於此者矣。
The Hall of Imperial Heaven is where the court assembles ministers and issues commands—the ancient Bright Hall. Yet disaster struck it first—an extraordinary omen. Unless Your Majesty examines yourself, extends grace broadly, reforms government, and relieves the destitute throughout the realm, Heaven's angry reproach cannot be turned aside. Earlier Imperial Academy students who, as sole surviving sons, petitioned to care for their parents were punished and sent to frontier garrison—this truly damages the dignity of governance. After the recent great amnesty, the judicial offices clung to routine statutes, and men who should have been freed were still held. I also beg that you cleanse these abuses anew, remit rents and levies, and levy nothing at all. Let all officials keep their salaries intact; select the worthy, carry out recommendations, and for greedy, corrupt officials who ruin government, examine their crimes and dismiss them. Then hearts will rejoice, harmony can be restored, and the ancestral altars secured—the foundation for the state's endurance through ten thousand years; nothing is greater than this.
12
且國家所恃以久長者，惟天命人心，而天命常視人心為去留。 今天意如此，不宜勞民。 當還都南京，奉謁陵廟，告以災變之故。 保養聖躬休息於無為。 毋聽小人之言，復有所興作，以誤陛下於後也。
What the state relies on for long endurance is Heaven's mandate and the people's hearts, and Heaven's mandate follows the people's hearts in staying or departing. Today Heaven's intent is clear; the people ought not to be burdened further. You should return the capital to Nanjing, pay respects at the imperial tombs and temples, and report the reason for this calamity. Nurture your sacred person and rest in non-action. Do not heed petty men's counsel and launch new works, lest Your Majesty be led astray hereafter.
13
書奏，不省。
The memorial was submitted, but the throne took no notice.
14
時三殿初成，帝方以定都詔天下，忽罹火災，頗懼，下詔求直言。 及言者多斥時政，帝不懌，而大臣復希旨詆言者。 帝於是發怒，謂言事者謗訕，下詔嚴禁之，犯者不赦。 侍讀李時勉、侍講羅汝敬俱下獄； 御史鄭維桓、何忠、羅通、徐容，給事中柯暹俱左官交阯。 惟緝與主事高公望、庶吉士楊復得無罪。 是年冬，緝進右庶子兼侍講。 明年九月卒於官。
The three main halls had just been completed; the Emperor had just proclaimed the fixing of the capital when fire suddenly struck. Alarmed, he issued an edict calling for frank counsel. When many memorials condemned current policy, the Emperor was displeased, and senior ministers again curried favor by attacking the critics. The Emperor thereupon grew angry, declaring that critics were slandering the throne, and issued an edict strictly forbidding such speech; offenders would not be pardoned. Reader-in-Waiting Li Shimian and Reader-in-Waiting Luo Rujing were both imprisoned; Censors Zheng Weiheng, He Zhong, Luo Tong, and Xu Rong, and Supervising Secretary Ke Xian were all demoted and sent to Jiaozhi. Only Zou Ji, Chief Clerk Gao Gongwang, and Hanlin Bachelor Yang Fu escaped punishment. That winter Zou Ji was promoted to Right Vice-Director of the Household and concurrently Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting. The following September he died in office.
15
緝博極群書，居官勤慎，清操如寒士。 子循，宣德中為翰林待詔，請贈父母。 帝諭吏部曰：「曩皇祖征沙漠，朕守北京，緝在左右，陳說皆正道，良臣也，其予之。」
Zou Ji had mastered every branch of learning, served with diligence and care, and maintained the pure integrity of a poor scholar. His son Xun served as a Hanlin awaiting imperial decree during the Xuande reign and petitioned for posthumous honors for his parents. The Emperor told the Ministry of Personnel: "When my imperial ancestor campaigned in the desert and I held Beijing, Zou Ji was at my side. Everything he counseled was sound—he is a worthy minister. Grant his request."
16
鄭維桓，慈溪人。 永樂十三年進士。 出知交阯南清州，卒。 柯暹，池州建德人。 由鄉舉出知交阯州。 累官浙江、雲南按察使。
Zheng Weiheng came from Cixi. He passed the palace examination in Yongle 13 (1415). He was sent out as prefect of Nanqing Prefecture in Jiaozhi, where he died. Ke Xian came from Jiande in Chizhou. Through the provincial examination he was sent out as prefect of Jiaozhi Prefecture. He rose through the ranks to serve as Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang and Yunnan.
17
弋謙，代州人。 永樂九年進士。 除監察御史。 出按江西，言事忤旨，貶峽山知縣。 復坐事免歸。
Yi Qian came from Daizhou. He passed the palace examination in Yongle 9 (1411). He was appointed Investigating Censor. Sent to inspect Jiangxi, he memorialized on affairs in a way that offended the throne and was demoted to magistrate of Xiashan. He was again dismissed over an affair and returned home.
18
仁宗在東宮，素知謙骨鯁。 及嗣位，召為大理少卿。 直陳時政，言官吏貪殘，政事多非洪武之舊，及有司誅求無藝。 帝多采納。 既復言五事，詞太激，帝乃不懌。 尚書呂震、吳中，侍郎吳廷用，大理卿虞謙等因劾謙誣罔，都御史劉觀令眾御史合糾謙。 帝召楊士奇等言之，士奇對曰：「謙不諳大體，然心感超擢恩，欲圖報耳。 主聖則臣直，惟陛下優容之。 」帝乃不罪謙。 然每見謙，詞色甚厲。 士奇從容言：「陛下詔求直言，謙言不當，觸怒。 外廷悚惕，以言為戒。 今四方朝覲之臣皆集闕下，見謙如此，將謂陛下不能容直言。 」帝惕然曰：「此固朕不能容，亦呂震輩迎合以益朕過，自今當置之。 」遂免謙朝參，令專視司事。
While Emperor Ren was heir apparent, he had long known Yi Qian's uncompromising integrity. When he succeeded to the throne, Yi Qian was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review. He spoke forthrightly on current affairs, declaring that officials were greedy and cruel, that government had largely departed from Hongwu practice, and that local offices extorted without restraint. The Emperor largely adopted his recommendations. When he again raised five matters, his language was too harsh and the Emperor was displeased. Ministers Lu Zhen and Wu Zhong, Vice Minister Wu Tingyong, Court of Judicial Review Minister Yu Qian, and others thereupon impeached Yi Qian for deceit, and Censor-in-Chief Liu Guan ordered the censors jointly to impeach him. The Emperor summoned Yang Shiqi and others to discuss the matter. Shiqi replied: "Yi Qian does not grasp the larger pattern, yet his heart is moved by the grace of his sudden promotion and he wishes to repay it. When the ruler is sage, ministers speak straight; I beg Your Majesty to be indulgent toward him. " The Emperor thereupon did not punish Yi Qian. Yet whenever he saw Yi Qian, his words and manner were very harsh. Shiqi said calmly: "Your Majesty issued an edict seeking forthright speech. Yi Qian spoke inappropriately and provoked Your Majesty's anger. The outer court is fearful and wary, taking speech as a warning. Officials from all quarters are now gathered below the palace gate. Seeing Yi Qian treated thus, they will conclude that Your Majesty cannot tolerate forthright speech. " The Emperor said soberly: "This is indeed my failure to be tolerant, and Lu Zhen and his ilk have curried favor and added to my fault. From now on I should set this aside. " Thereupon Yi Qian was exempted from court attendance and ordered to concentrate solely on his official duties.
19
未幾，帝以言事者益少，復召士奇曰：「朕怒謙矯激過實耳，朝臣遂月餘無言。 爾語諸臣，白朕心。 」士奇曰：「臣空言不足信，乞親降璽書。 」遂令就榻前書敕引過曰：「朕自即位以來，臣民上章以數百計，未嘗不欣然聽納。 茍有不當，不加譴訶，群臣所共知也。 間者，大理少卿弋謙所言，多非實事，群臣迎合朕意，交章奏其賣直，請置諸法。 朕皆拒而不聽，但免謙朝參。 而自是以來，言者益少。 今自去冬無雪，春亦少雨，陰陽愆和，必有其咎，豈無可言？ 而為臣者，懷自全之計，退而默默，何以為忠？ 朕于謙一時不能含容，未嘗不自愧咎。 爾群臣勿以前事為戒，於國家利弊、政令未當者，直言勿諱。 謙朝參如故。 」時中官采木四川，貪橫。 帝以謙清直，命往治之。 擢謙副都御史，賜鈔以行，遂罷采木之役。
Before long, seeing that fewer officials were speaking up, the Emperor again summoned Shiqi and said: "My anger at Yi Qian was only over his exaggeration and excess, yet court officials went more than a month without speaking. Speak to the officials and explain my intent. " Shiqi said: "My words alone will not be believed. I beg that Your Majesty personally issue an imperial letter. " He was then ordered to draft at the bedside an edict acknowledging fault, which read: "Since I ascended the throne, officials and commoners have submitted memorials numbering in the hundreds, and I have never failed to hear and accept them gladly. When any were inappropriate, I did not add rebuke—all the officials know this. Recently Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Yi Qian spoke much that was not factual. Officials curried my favor and jointly memorialized that he was selling integrity and asked that he be punished by law. I refused all of this, but only exempted Yi Qian from court attendance. Yet since then, those who speak up have grown fewer still. Now since last winter there has been no snow and spring too has had little rain. Yin and yang are out of harmony—there must be some fault. Can there truly be nothing worth saying? Yet as ministers, if you harbor plans for self-preservation and withdraw in silence, how is that loyalty? Toward Yi Qian I could not for a time contain myself, and I have never ceased to feel ashamed. You officials must not take the previous affair as a warning. Where the state's interests are at stake or policy is wrong, speak forthrightly without reserve. Yi Qian's court attendance is restored as before. " At the time eunuchs were procuring timber in Sichuan, acting with greed and overbearing violence. Because Yi Qian was pure and upright, the Emperor ordered him to go and put a stop to it. Yi Qian was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, given paper money for the journey, and the timber-procurement corvée was thereupon abolished.
20
宣德初，交阯右布政戚遜以貪淫黜，命謙往代。 王通棄交阯，謙亦論死。 正統初，釋為民。 土木之變，謙布衣走闕下，薦通及寧懋、阮遷等十三人，皆奇才可用。 眾議以通副石亨，謙請專任通，事遂寢。 廷臣以謙負重名，奏留之，亦不報。 景泰二年復至京，疏薦通等，不納。 罷歸，未幾卒。 仁宗性寬大，容直言，謙以故得無罪，反責呂震等。 而黃驥言西域事，帝亦誚震而行其言。
At the beginning of the Xuande reign, Right Provincial Administrator of Jiaozhi Qi Xun was dismissed for greed and licentiousness, and Yi Qian was ordered to replace him. When Wang Tong abandoned Jiaozhi, Yi Qian was also sentenced to death. At the beginning of the Zhengtong reign he was released to live as a commoner. At the Tumu crisis, Yi Qian in commoner's garb hurried to the palace gate and recommended Wang Tong, Ning Mao, Ruan Qian, and thirteen others in all—extraordinary talents fit for service. The assembly debated making Wang Tong deputy to Shi Heng, but Yi Qian asked that Tong be given sole responsibility, and the matter lapsed. Court officials, because Yi Qian bore a great reputation, memorialized to retain him, but this too received no response. In Jingtai 2 (1451) he again came to the capital and submitted a memorial recommending Wang Tong and others, but it was not accepted. He resigned and returned home, and soon died. Emperor Ren was by nature magnanimous and tolerated forthright speech; Yi Qian for this reason escaped punishment, and the Emperor instead blamed Lu Zhen and others. When Huang Ji spoke on Western Regions affairs, the Emperor also rebuked Lu Zhen and carried out Ji's recommendations.
21
驥，全州人。 洪武中，中鄉舉。 為沙縣教諭。 永樂時擢禮科給事中，常三使西域。 仁宗初，上疏言：「西域貢使多商人假托，無賴小人投為從者，乘傳役人，運貢物至京師，賞賚優厚。 番人慕利，貢無虛月，致民失業妨農。 比其使還，多賫貨物，車運至百餘輛。 丁男不足，役及婦女。 所至辱驛官，鞭夫隸，無敢與較者。 乞敕陜西行都司，惟哈密諸國王遣使入貢者，許令來京，止正副使得乘驛馬，陜人庶少蘇。 至西域所產，惟馬切邊需，應就給甘肅軍士。 其碙砂、梧桐、鹼之類，皆無益國用，請一切勿受，則來者自稀，浮費益省。 」帝以示尚書呂震，且讓之曰：「驥嘗奉使，悉西事。 卿西人，顧不悉邪？ 驥言是，其即議行。 」後遷右通政，與李琦、羅汝敬撫諭交阯，不辱命。 使還，尋卒。
Huang Ji came from Quanzhou. During the Hongwu reign he passed the provincial examination. He served as instructor of Shaxian. In the Yongle reign he was promoted to Supervising Secretary of the Ritual Section and was thrice sent as envoy to the Western Regions. At the beginning of Emperor Ren's reign, he submitted a memorial saying: "Western Regions tribute envoys are mostly merchants falsely posing as such. Worthless petty men attach themselves as followers, commandeer relay horses and press men into service, transport tribute goods to the capital, and receive generous rewards. The frontier peoples covet profit, and tribute missions come nearly every month, causing the people to lose their livelihoods and hampering agriculture. When their envoys return, they mostly carry goods away in more than a hundred carts. When adult males are insufficient, corvée labor extends even to women. Wherever they go they humiliate relay officials and whip laborers and clerks, and none dare stand up to them. I beg that the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission be ordered: only when kings of states such as Hami send envoys to offer tribute should they be permitted to come to the capital, and only the chief and deputy envoys should be allowed relay horses—so that the people of Shaanxi may breathe somewhat easier. Of Western Regions products, only horses are urgently needed on the frontier; these should be distributed directly to the Gansu garrison troops. Sal ammoniac, parasol trees, alkali, and the like all benefit state use not at all. I ask that none of these be accepted—then visitors will naturally grow scarce and wasteful expenditure be further reduced. " The Emperor showed the memorial to Minister Lu Zhen and rebuked him, saying: "Huang Ji has served on missions and knows Western affairs thoroughly. You are a native of the west—do you not know these matters? Huang Ji's words are correct. Deliberate at once and implement them. " Later he was transferred to Right Administrator and, together with Li Qi and Luo Rujing, went to pacify and instruct Jiaozhi without disgracing the commission. After completing the mission and returning, he soon died.
22
黃澤，閩縣人。 永樂十年進士。 擢河南左參政。 南陽多流民，拊循使復業。 嘗率丁役至北京，周恤備至。 久之，調湖廣。 仁宗即位，入覲，言時政，多見采。
Huang Ze came from Min County. He passed the palace examination in Yongle 10 (1412). He was promoted to Left Provincial Administrator of Henan. Nanyang had many displaced persons; he comforted and guided them back to their occupations. Once when he led corvée laborers to Beijing, he showed them every consideration. After a long time he was transferred to Huguang. When Emperor Ren ascended the throne, he came to audience, spoke on current affairs, and much of what he said was adopted.
23
宣宗立，下詔求言。 澤上疏言正心、恤民、敬天、納諫、練兵、重農、止貢獻、明賞罰、遠嬖幸、汰冗官十事。 其言遠嬖幸曰：「刑余之人，其情幽陰，其慮險譎。 大奸似忠，大詐似信，大巧似愚。 一與之親，如飲醇酒，不知其醉； 如噬甘臘，不知其毒。 寵之甚易，遠之甚難。 是以古者宦寺不使典兵幹政，所以防患於未萌也。 涓涓弗塞，將為江河。 此輩宜一切疏遠，勿使用事。 漢、唐已事，彰彰可監。 」當成祖時，宦官稍稍用事，宣宗浸以親幸。 澤於十事中此為尤切。 帝雖嘉嘆，不能用也。 其後設內書堂，而中人多通書曉文義。 宦寺之盛，自宣宗始。
When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, he issued an edict seeking counsel. Huang Ze submitted a memorial on ten matters: rectifying the heart, caring for the people, reverencing Heaven, accepting remonstrance, drilling troops, valuing agriculture, halting tribute offerings, clarifying rewards and punishments, keeping distance from favorites, and eliminating redundant officials. On keeping distance from favorites he said: "Men punished by mutilation have dispositions that are dark and hidden and designs that are treacherous. Great treachery resembles loyalty, great deceit resembles faithfulness, and great cunning resembles foolishness. Once you grow close to them, it is like drinking fine wine without knowing you are drunk; it is like eating sweet cured meat without knowing its poison. To favor them is very easy; to keep them at a distance is very hard. Therefore in antiquity palace eunuchs were not allowed to command troops or meddle in government—this was to guard against trouble before it sprouted. A trickle left unblocked becomes a river. This sort should all be kept at a distance and not employed in affairs of state. The precedents of Han and Tang stand plain and may serve as mirrors. " During the Yongle Emperor's reign eunuchs gradually began to wield power, and Emperor Xuanzong increasingly favored them. Among the ten matters, this was Huang Ze's most pointed counsel. The Emperor praised and sighed over it, but could not put it into practice. Afterward the Inner Calligraphy Hall was established, and eunuchs mostly mastered writing and understood literary meaning. The great flourishing of palace eunuchs began with Emperor Xuanzong.
24
宣德三年擢浙江布政使。 復上言平陽、麗水等七縣銀冶宜罷，並請盡罷諸坑冶，語甚切。 帝嘆息曰：「民困若此，朕何由知？ 遣官驗視，酌議以聞。 」澤在官有政績，然多暴怒，鹽運使丁鎡不避道，撻之，為所奏。 巡按御史馬謹亦劾澤九載秩滿，自出行縣，斂白金三千兩償官物，且越境過家。 遂逮下獄。 正統六年黜為民。 初，澤奏金華、臺州戶口較洪武時耗減，而歲造弓箭如舊，乞減免。 下部議得允，而澤已罷官逾月矣。
In Xuande 3 (1428) he was promoted to Provincial Administrator of Zhejiang. He again memorialized that the silver smelteries of the seven counties including Pingyang and Lishui ought to be abolished, and also asked that all mining operations be wholly abolished; his language was very pointed. The Emperor sighed and said: "The people are in such distress—how am I to know? Send officials to inspect and verify, discuss appropriate measures, and report back. " While serving in office, Ze had administrative achievements, yet he was often violently angry; the Salt Transport Commissioner Ding Zan did not yield the road and was flogged, and Ze was impeached for it. The touring investigating censor Ma Jin also impeached Ze: after nine years his term was complete, he went out personally to inspect the counties, collected three thousand taels of white silver to repay official goods, and moreover crossed district boundaries to visit his home. He was thereupon arrested and imprisoned. In Zhengtong 6 (1441) he was dismissed and reduced to commoner status. Previously, Ze had memorialized that the registered population of Jinhua and Taizhou had declined compared to the Hongwu era, while the annual manufacture of bows and arrows remained unchanged, and he begged for reduction and exemption. The ministry deliberated and approval was granted, but Ze had already been removed from office for more than a month.
25
孔友諒，長洲人。 永樂十六年進士。 改庶吉士，出知雙流縣。 宣宗初，上言六事：
Kong Youliang came from Changzhou. He passed the jinshi examination in Yongle 16 (1418). He was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, then sent out as magistrate of Shuangliu County. At the beginning of Emperor Xuanzong's reign, he submitted a memorial on six matters:
26
一曰，守令親民之官，古者不拘資格，必得其人； 不限歲月，使盡其力。 今居職者多不知撫字之方，而廉幹得民心者，又遷調不常，差遣不一。 或因小事連累，朝夕營治，往來道路，日不暇給。 乞敕吏部，擇才望素優及久歷京官者任之。 諭戒上司，毋擅差遣，假以歲月，責成治效。 至遠缺佐貳，多經裁減，獨員居職。 或遇事赴京，多委雜職署事，因循茍且，政令無常，民不知畏。 今後路遠之缺，常留一正員任事，不得擅離，庶法有常守。
First, prefects and magistrates are officials close to the people; in antiquity they did not rigidly bound by qualifications—they had to obtain the right person; Without limiting their term in months, they were made to exert their full strength. Today those holding office mostly do not know how to comfort and nourish the people, while those who are incorrupt, capable, and win the people's hearts are transferred irregularly and dispatched on various assignments. Sometimes they are implicated over minor matters, managing affairs morning and evening and traveling back and forth on the roads, with scarcely a moment to spare. I beg that the Ministry of Personnel be ordered to select those of outstanding talent and reputation and those long experienced in capital office to appoint them. Admonish and warn their superiors not to dispatch them on their own authority, grant them sufficient time, and hold them accountable for governing achievements. As for distant deputy posts, many have been cut by reductions, leaving a single incumbent to hold the position alone. Sometimes when urgent business requires a trip to the capital, many entrust miscellaneous subordinates to act in their stead—procrastinating perfunctorily, government orders without constancy, and the people unaware of what to fear. From now on, for distant vacancies, regularly leave one regular incumbent in charge of affairs, who may not leave without authorization—then the law will have a constant guardian.
27
二曰，科舉所以求賢，必名實相副，非徒誇多而已。 今秋闈取士動一二百人。 弊既多端，僥幸過半。 會試下第，十常八九，其登第者，實行或乖。 請於開科之歲，詳核諸生行履。 孝弟忠信、學業優贍者，乃許入試。 庶浮薄不致濫收，而國家得真才之用。
Second, the civil service examinations are meant to seek the worthy—they must match name and reality, not merely boast of quantity. Today at the autumn provincial examinations, one or two hundred scholars are selected. Abuses are manifold; more than half pass by sheer luck. Of those who fail the metropolitan examination, eight or nine out of ten; of those who pass, actual conduct is often at odds. I ask that in years when examinations are held, the conduct and records of students be thoroughly verified. Only those filial, respectful to elders, loyal, trustworthy, and superior in learning and substance may be permitted to enter the examination. Then the frivolous and shallow will not be indiscriminately enrolled, and the state will obtain the employment of true talent.
28
三曰，祿以養廉，祿入過薄，則生事不給。 國朝制祿之典，視前代為薄。 今京官及方面官稍增俸祿，其餘大小官自折鈔外，月不過米二石，不足食數人。 仰事俯育，與道路往來，費安所取資？ 貪者放利行私，廉者終窶莫訴。 請敕戶部勘實天下糧儲，以歲支之余，量增官俸。 仍令內外風憲官，采訪廉潔之吏，重加旌賞。 則廉者知勸，貪者知戒。
Third, salary is to nurture integrity—if salary income is too meager, then daily needs cannot be met. Our dynasty's system of salary allotments is thin compared to previous ages. Today capital officials and regional officials have had their salaries somewhat increased; the remaining officials large and small, apart from converted paper money, receive no more than two shi of rice per month—not enough to feed several people. Supporting parents above and nurturing children below, and traveling on the roads—where does the money come from? The greedy profit privately through usury; the incorrupt end destitute with no one to whom they can appeal. I ask that the Ministry of Revenue be ordered to verify truthfully the grain stores throughout the realm, and from the surplus of annual disbursements, measure an increase to official salaries. Also order internal and external circuit censors to investigate and commend incorrupt officials with substantial rewards. Then the incorrupt will know encouragement, and the greedy will know warning.
29
四曰，古者賦役量土宜，驗丁口，不責所無，不盡所有。 今自常賦外，復有和買、采辦諸事。 自朝廷視之，不過令有司支官錢平買。 而無賴之輩，關通吏胥，壟斷貨物，巧立辨驗、折耗之名，科取數倍，奸弊百端。 乞盡停采買，減諸不急務，則國賦有常，民無科擾。
Fourth, in antiquity taxes and corvée were measured to local suitability and verified by household registers—not demanding what was not had, not exhausting all that was possessed. Today beyond the regular taxes, there are again cooperative purchasing, procurement, and various other matters. From the court's perspective, it is merely ordering local officials to disburse official funds to purchase at fair prices. But rascals collude with clerks and runners, monopolize goods, ingeniously establish names such as verification and loss allowance, levying several times the amount—abuses of every kind. I beg that procurement be wholly halted and various non-urgent affairs reduced—then state levies will have constancy and the people will be free from irregular exactions.
30
其二事言汰冗員，任風憲，言者多及之，不具載。
His other two items spoke of eliminating redundant posts and appointing circuit censors—many memorialists also touched on these; they are not fully recorded here.
31
宣德八年，命吏部擇外官有文學者六十八人試之，得友諒及進士胡端禎等七人，悉令辦事六科。 居二年，皆授給事中，惟友諒未授官而卒。
In Xuande 8 (1433) the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to select sixty-eight external officials of literary accomplishment to test them; Youliang was obtained, together with jinshi Hu Duanzhen and six others—all were ordered to handle affairs in the Six Offices of Scrutiny. After two years, all were appointed supervising secretaries; only Youliang died before receiving appointment.
32
範濟，元進士。 洪武中，以文學舉為廣信知府，坐累謫戍興州。 宣宗即位，濟年八十餘矣，詣闕言八事：
Fan Ji was a jinshi of the Yuan. In the Hongwu era he was recommended for literary accomplishment and appointed Prefect of Guangxin; implicated in a case he was banished to garrison duty at Xingzhou. When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, Ji was already over eighty; he came to the palace gates and submitted a memorial on eight matters:
33
其一曰楮幣之法，昉於漢、唐。 元造元統交鈔，後又造中統鈔。 久而物重鈔輕，公私俱敝，乃造至元鈔與中統鈔兼行。 子母相權，新陳通用。 又令民間以昏鈔赴平準庫，中統鈔五貫得換至元鈔一貫。 又其法日造萬錠，共計官吏俸稍、內府供用若干，天下正稅雜課若干，斂發有方，周流不滯，以故久而通行。 太祖皇帝造大明寶鈔。 以鈔一貫當白金一兩，民歡趨之。 迄今五十餘年，其法稍弊，亦由物重鈔輕所致。 願陛下因時變通，重造寶鈔，一準洪武初制，使新舊兼行。 取元時所造之數而增損之，審國家度支之數而權衡之。 俾鈔少而物多，鈔重而物輕。 嚴偽造之條，開倒換之法，推陳出新，無耗無阻，則鈔法流通，永永無弊。
The first spoke of the method of paper currency, which began in Han and Tang. The Yuan minted Yuantong Jiaochao, and later also minted Zhongtong Chao. After a long time goods were heavy and notes light—public and private alike were exhausted; they then minted Zhiyuan Chao to circulate jointly with Zhongtong Chao. Parent and child notes counterbalanced each other; new and old were universally used. They also ordered the people to bring worn notes to the Stabilization Office—five strings of Zhongtong Chao could be exchanged for one string of Zhiyuan Chao. Furthermore their law minted ten thousand ingots daily; totaling official salaries, inner-palace supplies, regular taxes and miscellaneous levies throughout the realm—collection and issuance had method, circulation without stagnation; for this reason it circulated for long. Emperor Hongwu minted the Da Ming Treasure Note. One note string equaled one tael of white silver; the people gladly rushed to use it. To this day more than fifty years have passed—the method has slightly deteriorated, also because goods are heavy and notes light. I wish Your Majesty, adapting to circumstances and changing with the times, would remint Treasure Notes according to the initial Hongwu system, making new and old circulate jointly. Take the quantity minted in Yuan times and increase or decrease it; examine the state's expenditure figures and weigh them. Thus notes would be few and goods many, notes heavy and goods light. Strictly enforce provisions against counterfeiting, open methods of exchange, pushing out the old and bringing in the new—without loss, without obstruction—then the note system would circulate, forever without defect.
34
其二曰備邊之道，守險為要。 若朔州、大同、開平、宣府、大寧，乃京師之藩垣，邊僥之門戶。 士可耕，城可守。 宜盛兵防禦，廣開屯田，修治城堡，謹烽火，明斥堠。 毋貪小利，毋輕遠求，堅壁清野，使無所得。 俟其憊而擊之，得利則止，毋窮追深入。 此守邊大要也。
The second spoke of the way to prepare the frontier—holding perilous passes is essential. Such as Shuozhou, Datong, Kaiping, Xuanfu, and Daning—these are the bulwark of the capital, the gateways of the border marches. The land can be cultivated; the cities can be defended. It is fit to mass troops for defense, broadly open garrison farming, repair and maintain fortresses, carefully maintain beacon fires, and make clear the outpost stations. Do not covet small profit, do not lightly seek far—fortify walls and clear the countryside, so they obtain nothing. Wait until they are weary and then strike; if profit is gained then stop—do not pursue deeply. This is the great gist of guarding the frontier.
35
其三曰兵不在多，在於堪戰。 比者多發為事官吏人民充軍塞上，非白面書生，則老弱病廢。 遇有征行，有力者得免，貧弱者備數。 器械不完，糗糧不具。 望風股栗，安能效死？ 今宜選其壯勇，勤加訓練，余但令乘城擊柝，趨走牙門，庶幾各得其用。
The third says troops are not in quantity but in being fit for battle. Recently many officials and people involved in cases have been sent to fill military service on the frontier—if not pale-faced bookish scholars, then old, weak, sick, and disabled. When there is a campaign, the strong can avoid it; the poor and weak fill the numbers. Weapons incomplete; dried rations not provided. At the sight of the enemy they tremble in their legs—how can they be expected to fight to the death? Now it is fit to select the stalwart and brave and train them diligently; the rest need only be ordered to mount the walls and strike the night-watch clapper and run to the gate headquarters—then each will mostly obtain his use.
36
其四曰民病莫甚於勾軍。 衛所差官至六七員，百戶差軍旗亦二三人，皆有力交結及畏避征調之徒，重賄得遣。 既至州縣，擅作威福，迫脅裏甲，恣為奸私。 無丁之家，誅求不已； 有丁之戶，詐稱死亡。 托故留滯，久而不還。 及還，則以所得財物，遍賄官吏，朦朧具覆。 究其所取之丁，十不得一，欲軍無缺伍難矣。 自今軍士有故，令各衛報都督府及兵部，府、部諜布政、按察司。 令府州縣準籍貫姓名，勾取送衛，則差人騷擾之弊自絕。
The fourth says no suffering of the people is greater than military household conscription verification. Guard posts send as many as six or seven officials; company commanders send two or three military bannermen—all are men with powerful connections and those who fear and evade levies, obtaining dispatch through heavy bribes. Once they arrive at prefecture and county, they arbitrarily wield authority, coerce the tithing heads, and indulge in private wrongdoing. Households without quota sons are extorted without end; households with quota sons falsely claim death. Using excuses they delay and linger, long without returning. When they return, they use the goods obtained to bribe officials everywhere, and muddle through with perfunctory reports. Investigating the quota sons actually taken—ten do not yield one; to wish the army without depleted ranks is difficult indeed. From now when soldiers have affairs, order each guard to report to the Chief Military Commission and Ministry of War; the commission and ministry notify the provincial administration and surveillance commissions. Order prefectures, departments, and counties according to registered domicile and name to conscript and deliver to the guard—then the abuse of dispatching personnel causing harassment will of itself cease.
37
其五曰洪武中令軍士七分屯田，三分守城，最為善策。 比者調度日繁，興造日廣，虛有屯種之名，田多荒蕪。 兼養馬、采草、伐薪、燒炭，雜役旁午，兵力焉得不疲、農業焉得不廢？ 願敕邊將課卒墾荒，限以頃畝，官給牛種，稽其勤惰，明賞罰以示勸懲。 則塞下田可盡墾，轉餉益紓，諸邊富實，計無便於此者。
The fifth says in the Hongwu era it was ordered that soldiers seven parts garrison-farm, three parts guard the city—the most excellent policy. Recently transfers and deployments have grown frequent, construction daily expands—there is only the name of garrison planting, while fields are mostly abandoned. Added to raising horses, gathering fodder, cutting firewood, burning charcoal—miscellaneous corvée duties at every turn—how can military strength not be exhausted, how can agriculture not be abandoned? I wish the frontier generals be ordered to compel troops to reclaim wasteland, limit by qing and mu, the state provide oxen and seed, examine their diligence and slackness, and clearly display rewards and punishments to show encouragement and warning. Then frontier fields can be fully reclaimed, transport of grain will be further eased, the various frontiers rich and solid—no plan is more convenient than this.
38
其六曰，學校者，風化之源，人材所自出，貴明體適用，非徒較文藝而已也。 洪武中妙選師儒，教養甚備，人材彬彬可觀。 邇來士習委靡，立志不弘，執節不固。 平居無剛方正大之氣，安望其立朝為名公卿哉！ 宜選良士為郡縣學官，擇民間子弟性行端謹者為生徒，訓以經史，勉以節行。 俟其有成，貢於國學。 磨礱砥礪，使其氣充誌定，卓然成材，然後舉而用之，以任天下國家事無難矣。
The sixth says schools are the source of moral transformation, where talent issues forth—it is prized to clarify substance and fit for application, not merely to compare literary accomplishments. In the Hongwu era teachers and scholars were wondrously selected, nurturing and training very complete—talent flourished and was splendid to behold. Recently scholars' habits have declined, aspirations not broad, integrity of conduct not firm. In ordinary life without stern, upright, and grand spirit—how can one look to them to stand at court as eminent ministers and grand counsellors! It is fit to select worthy scholars as prefectural and county school officers, select among the common people's sons those upright and careful in character as students, instruct them in the Classics and histories, and exhort them in integrity of conduct. Wait until they have achieved mastery, then present them to the National University. Grind and temper them, making their spirit full and resolve set, standing out as accomplished talent—then raise and employ them; to entrust them with affairs of the realm under Heaven and the state would be without difficulty.
39
其七曰兵者凶器，聖人不得已而用之。 漢高祖解平城之圍，未聞蕭、曹勸以復仇； 唐太宗禦突厥於便橋，未聞房、杜勸以報怨。 古英君良相不欲疲民力以誇武功，計慮遠矣。 洪武初年嘗赫然命將，欲清沙漠。 既以饋運不繼，旋即頒師。 遂撤東勝衛於大同，塞山西陽武谷口，選將練兵，扼險以待。 內修政教，外嚴邊備，廣屯田，興學校，罪貪吏，徙頑民。 不數年間，朵兒只巴獻女，伯顏帖木兒、乃兒不花等相繼擒獲，納哈出亦降。 此專務內治，不勤遠略之明效也。 伏望遠鑒漢、唐，近法太祖，毋以窮兵黷武為快，毋以犁庭掃穴為功。 棄捐不毛之地，休養冠帶之民，俾竭力於田桑，盡心於庠序。 邊塞絕傷痍之苦，閭里絕呻吟之聲。 將無幸功，士無夭閼，遠人自服，荒外自歸。 國祚靈長於萬年矣。
The seventh says arms are inauspicious instruments—the sage uses them only when unavoidable. Han Gaozu resolved the siege at Pingcheng—one did not hear Xiao He and Cao Can urge revenge; Tang Taizong repelled the Turks at Bianqiao—one did not hear Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui urge repaying grudges. Ancient worthy rulers and good ministers did not wish to exhaust the people's strength to boast military achievements—their calculation and consideration were far-reaching indeed. In the early Hongwu era they once majestically ordered generals, wishing to clear the desert wastes. Since supply transport could not continue, they immediately withdrew the army. They then withdrew the Dongsheng Guard to Datong, blocked the Yangwu Pass in Shanxi, selected generals and trained troops, and held perilous passes to await the enemy. Internally they cultivated government and education, externally they tightened frontier defenses, broadly expanded garrison farming, established schools, punished greedy officials, and relocated obstinate commoners. Within a few years Duoyinashiba presented his daughter, Boyan Temür, Naibuhua, and others were captured in succession, and Nahachu also surrendered. This is the clear effect of devoting oneself to internal governance and not zealously pursuing distant strategies. I humbly hope Your Majesty will take Han and Tang as distant mirrors and Emperor Hongwu as the near model—do not take exhausting the army and abusing military force as pleasure, do not take uprooting the enemy's nest and sweeping their lair as achievement. Abandon barren lands, rest and nurture the civilized people, make them exert their strength in fields and mulberry, and devote their hearts to schools. The frontier passes will be free of the suffering of wounds, and the villages free of the sounds of groaning. Generals will not hope for lucky achievements, scholars will not die young and frustrated, distant peoples will of themselves submit, and the wild beyond will of themselves return. The dynastic fortune will be numinously enduring for ten thousand years.
40
其八曰官不在眾，在乎得人。 國家承大亂後，因時損益，以府為州，以州為縣。 繼又裁並小縣之糧不及俸者，量民數以設官。 民多者縣設丞薄，少者知縣、典史而已。 其時官無廢事，民不愁勞。 今藩、臬二司及府、州、縣官，視洪武中再倍，政愈不理，民愈不寧，奸弊叢生，詐偽滋起。 甚有官不能聽斷，吏不諳文移，乃容留書寫之人，在官影射，賄賂公行，獄訟淹滯，皆官冗吏濫所致也。 望斷自宸衷，凡內外官吏，並依洪武中員額，冗濫者悉汰，則天工無曠，庶績咸熙，而天下大治矣。
The eighth says officials are not in multitude but in obtaining the right persons. The state, inheriting after great disorder, increased and decreased according to the times—making prefectures into departments, departments into counties. Subsequently they also cut and merged small counties whose grain revenue did not reach official salaries, measuring population numbers to establish officials. Where population was large the county had assistant magistrate and registrar; where small, only the magistrate and archivist. At that time officials had no neglected affairs, and the people did not worry over toil. Today the two provincial commissions and prefectural, departmental, and county officials are twice those of the Hongwu era—government grows more ungoverned, the people more unsettled, abuses cluster and multiply, and fraud and falsehood flourish. Some officials cannot even hear and decide cases, clerks do not understand documents—yet they retain copyists who act in the officials' shadow at court, bribery runs openly, lawsuits stagnate—all caused by redundant officials and excessive clerks. I hope Your Majesty will decide from the imperial heart: all internal and external officials alike should follow the Hongwu establishment quotas, and all redundant and excessive ones be eliminated—then no heavenly task will be vacant, all achievements will flourish, and the realm under Heaven will be greatly governed.
41
奏上，命廷臣議之。 尚書呂震以為文辭冗長，且事多已行，不足采。 帝曰：「所言甚有學識，多契朕心，當察其素履以聞。 」震乃言：「濟故元進士，曾守郡，坐事戍邊。 」帝曰：「惜哉斯人！ 令久淹行伍，今猶足用。 」震曰：「年老矣。 」帝曰：「國家用人，正須老成，但不宜任以繁劇。 」乃以濟為儒學訓導。
The memorial was submitted; the Emperor ordered court ministers to deliberate on it. Minister Lü Zhen considered the language verbose and lengthy, and moreover many matters had already been implemented—not worth adopting. The Emperor said: "What was said has great learning and knowledge, much accord with my heart—I should investigate his past conduct and report. " Zhen then said: "Ji is a former Yuan jinshi, once governed a prefecture, implicated in a case and banished to garrison the frontier. " The Emperor said: "What a pity, this man! Having long been submerged in the ranks, he is still usable today. " Zhen said: "He is old. " The Emperor said: "The state in employing men just needs seasoned experience—only he should not be assigned heavy and complex duties. " Ji was then appointed Confucian Instructor.
42
邇歲土木繁興，異端盛起，番僧絡驛，汙吏縱橫，相臣不正其非，御史不劾其罪，上下蒙蔽，民生雕瘵。 狡寇犯邊，上皇播越。 陛下枕戈嘗膽之秋，可不拔賢舉能，一新政治乎？ 昔宗、嶽為將，敵國不敢呼名； 韓、範鎮邊，西賊聞之破膽。 司馬光居相位，強鄰戒勿犯邊。 今文武大臣之有威名德望者，宜使典樞要，且延訪智術才能之士，布滿朝廷，則也先必畏服，而上皇可指日還矣。
In recent years civil engineering has flourished, heterodox teachings have risen in force, foreign monks fill the post stations, corrupt officials run rampant, chief ministers do not correct their wrongs, censors do not impeach their crimes—above and below conceal one another, and the people's livelihood is wasted and afflicted. Crafty bandits violated the frontier; the Retired Emperor was driven into exile. Your Majesty, in this season of sleeping on spears and tasting gall—can you not elevate the worthy and raise the capable, and renew government entirely? Formerly when Zong Ze and Yue Fei were generals, enemy states did not dare speak their names; Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan guarded the frontier—western bandits heard of them and their courage broke. When Sima Guang held the chancellor's position, powerful neighbors were warned not to violate the frontier. Today civil and military grand ministers with martial renown and moral prestige should be made to manage vital affairs, and moreover wise and capable men of talent should be sought and spread throughout the court—then Esen will surely fear and submit, and the Retired Emperor can return within days.
43
大臣，陽也； 宦寺，陰也。 君子，陽也； 小人，陰也。 近日食地震，陰盛陽微，謫見天地。 望陛下總攬乾綱，抑宦寺使不得預政，遏小人俾不得居位，則陰陽順而天變弭矣。 天下治亂，在君心邪正。 田獵是娛，宮室是侈，宦寺是狎，三者有一，足蠱君心。 願陛下涵養克治，多接賢士大夫，少親宦官宮妾，自能革奢靡，戒遊佚，而心無不正矣。
Grand ministers are yang; palace eunuchs are yin. The noble man is yang; the petty man is yin. Recently there were eclipses and earthquakes—yin flourishes and yang is weak; reproof appears from Heaven and Earth. I hope Your Majesty will gather the heavenly reins, suppress palace eunuchs so they may not participate in government, restrain petty men so they may not hold office—then yin and yang will be harmonious and heavenly portents will cease. Order and disorder under Heaven lie in whether the ruler's heart is perverse or upright. Field hunting as amusement, palaces as extravagance, palace eunuchs as intimacy—if any one of the three exists, it suffices to bewitch the ruler's heart. I wish Your Majesty would cultivate and restrain yourself, receive many worthy scholar-officials, and keep close company with eunuchs and palace women less often—then of yourself you can reform extravagance, guard against wandering and idleness, and your heart will be without perversity.
44
堯立謗木，恐人不言，所以聖； 秦除謚法，恐人議己，所以亡。 陛下廣從諫之量，旌直言之臣，則國家利弊，閭閻休戚，臣下無所顧忌，而言無不盡矣。 蘇子曰：「平居無犯顏敢諫之臣，則臨難必無仗節死義之士。 」願陛下恒念是言而審察之。
Yao erected a criticism post, fearing that people would not speak—therefore he was sage; Qin abolished posthumous title law, fearing that people would criticize them—therefore they perished. Your Majesty, broaden the capacity to accept remonstrance and commend ministers who speak directly—then regarding the state's benefits and harms and the neighborhoods' weal and woe, subordinates will have nothing to fear, and speech will be without reserve. Master Su said: "In ordinary times without ministers who risk offending the face and dare remonstrate, then in crisis there will surely be no men who uphold integrity and die for righteousness. " I wish Your Majesty would constantly keep this saying in mind and examine it carefully.
45
書奏，帝頗嘉納之。 後四年，讓登進士。 官知縣卒。 景泰二年，監生郭佑亦上書言兵事，略曰：
The memorial was submitted; the Emperor greatly praised and accepted it. Four years later, Rang passed the jinshi examination. He served as magistrate and died. In Jingtai 2, Supervising Student Guo You also submitted a memorial on military affairs, briefly saying:
46
逆寇犯順，上皇蒙塵，此千古非常之變，百世必報之仇也。 今使臣之來，動以數千，務驕蹇責望於我，而我乃隱忍姑息，致賊勢日張，我氣日索，求和與和，求戰與戰，是和戰之權，不在我而在賊也。 願陛下結人心，親賢良，以固國本，廣儲蓄，練將士，以壯國氣。 正分定名，裁之以義。 如桀驁侵軼，則提兵問罪。 使大漠之南，不敢有匹馬闌入，乃可保百年無虞。 不然西北力罷，東南財竭，不能一日安枕矣。 昨以國用耗乏，謀國大臣欲紓一時之急，令民納粟者賜冠帶。 今軍旅稍寧，行之如故。 農工商販之徒，不較賢愚，惟財是授。 驕親戚，誇鄉里，長非分之邪心。 贓汙吏罷退為民，欲掩閭黨之恥，納粟納草，冠帶而歸。 前以冒貨去職，今以輸貨得官，何以禁貪殘、重名爵？ 況天下統一，藏富在民，未至大不得已，而舉措如此，是以空乏啟寇心也。 章下廷議，格不行。
Rebellious bandits violated righteousness; the Retired Emperor suffered dust on his robes—this is a change without parallel in a thousand ages, a grudge that must be repaid for a hundred generations. Today when their envoys come, they number in the thousands, striving to be arrogant and demanding toward us—yet we forbear and indulge, causing the bandits' power to grow daily and our spirit to shrink daily; we seek peace and they grant peace, we seek war and they grant war—the power over peace and war is not in our hands but in the bandits'. I wish Your Majesty would unite people's hearts, draw close to the worthy and good to solidify the state's foundation, broadly store up reserves and train generals and troops to strengthen the state's spirit. Correctly fix roles and establish names, and cut them with righteousness. If they are arrogant and overbearing in violation, then raise troops to demand punishment. Make it so south of the great desert not a single horse dares stray across the border—then one can preserve a century without worry. Otherwise the northwest's strength will be exhausted, the southeast's wealth depleted—you cannot rest your head on a pillow for a single day. Recently because state revenue was depleted and exhausted, state-counseling grand ministers wishing to relieve a moment's urgency ordered that those who contributed grain be granted cap and belt. Now that the army is somewhat settled, it continues as before. Farmers, craftsmen, merchants, and peddlers—without comparing worthiness and foolishness, only wealth is granted office. They pride themselves before kin, boast in their villages, and nurture improper perverse hearts. Corrupt officials dismissed and returned to commoner status, wishing to cover the shame of their neighborhood and clan, contribute grain and fodder, and return with cap and belt. Previously removed from office for coveting goods, now obtaining office for delivering goods—how can one prohibit greed and cruelty and esteem noble titles? Moreover the realm under Heaven is unified, wealth stored lies with the people—it has not reached great unavoidable necessity, yet measures are such as this—it is using emptiness and exhaustion to open the bandits' hearts. The memorial was sent down for court deliberation; it was blocked and not implemented.
47
又有胡仲倫者，雲南鹽課提舉司吏目也。 緣事入都，會上皇北狩，也先欲妻以妹，上皇因遣廣寧伯劉安入言於帝。 仲倫上疏爭之，言：「今日事不可屈者有七。 降萬乘之尊，與諧婚媾，一也。 敵假和議，使我無備，二也。 必欲為姻，驕尊自大，三也。 索金帛，使我坐困，四也。 以送駕為名，乘機入犯，五也。 逼上皇手詔，誘取邊城，六也。 欲求山後之地，七也。 稍從其一，大事去矣。 曩上皇在位，王振專權。 忠諫者死，鯁直者戍； 君子見斥，小人驟遷。 章奏多決中旨，黑白混淆，邪正倒置。 閩、浙之寇方殷，瓦剌之釁大作。 陛下宜親賢遠奸，信賞必罰，通上情，達下誌。 賣國之奸無所投隙，倉卒之變末由發機，朝廷自此尊，天下自此安矣。 」帝嘉納焉。
There was also Hu Zhonglun, a clerk of the Yunnan Salt Tax Intendant's Office. Because of business he entered the capital; it happened that the Retired Emperor went north on hunt, Esen wished to marry him to his younger sister—the Retired Emperor therefore sent Guangning Earl Liu An to enter and speak to the Emperor. Zhonglun submitted a memorial disputing it, saying: "In today's affair there are seven matters on which one cannot yield. Lowering the dignity of the Son of Heaven to harmonize in marriage alliance—first. The enemy feigns peace talks, making us unprepared—second. Insisting on marriage, arrogant and self-important—third. Demanding gold and silk, making us sit in exhaustion—fourth. Under the name of escorting the Emperor, seizing the opportunity to invade—fifth. Compelling the Retired Emperor's hand-written edict, luring away frontier cities—sixth. Seeking the lands behind the mountains—seventh. Yield even slightly to one of them, and the great affair is lost. Formerly when the Retired Emperor was on the throne, Wang Zhen monopolized power. Those who loyally remonstrated died, the blunt and upright were banished to garrison; noble men were expelled, petty men were suddenly promoted. Memorials were mostly decided by secret imperial will—black and white confused, perverse and upright inverted. Bandits in Fujian and Zhejiang were just rampant; the Oirat provocation greatly erupted. Your Majesty should draw close to the worthy and keep distant from the wicked, trust rewards and surely punish, connect upper sentiments and reach lower wills. Traitors who sell the state will have nowhere to slip in, sudden crises will have no means to arise—the court from this will be honored, and the realm under Heaven from this will be secure. " The Emperor praised and accepted it.
48
又有華敏者，南京錦衣軍余也。 意氣慷慨，讀書通大義，憤王振亂國，與儕輩言輒裂眥怒詈。 景泰三年九月上書曰：
There was also Hua Min, a surplus soldier of the Nanjing Embroidered Uniform Guard. His spirit was bold and generous; in reading he understood great principles—indignant that Wang Zhen disturbed the state, when speaking with his peers he would split his eyes in anger and curse. In the ninth month of Jingtai 3 he submitted a memorial saying:
49
近年以來，內官袁琦、唐受、喜寧、王振專權害政，致國事傾危。 望陛下防微杜漸，總攬權綱，為子孫萬世法。 不然恐禍稔蕭墻，曹節、侯覽之害，復見於今日。 臣雖賤陋，不勝痛哭流涕。 謹以虐軍害民十事，為陛下痛切言之。 內官家積金銀珠玉，累室兼籯，從何而至？ 非內盜府藏，則外朘民膏。 害一也。 怙勢矜寵，占公侯邸舍，興作工役，勞擾軍民。 害二也。 家人外親，皆市井無籍之子，縱橫豪悍，任意作奸，納粟補官，貴賤淆雜。 害三也。 建造佛寺，耗費不貲，營一己之私，破萬家之產。 害四也。 廣置田莊，不入賦稅，寄戶郡縣，不受征徭，阡陌連亙，而民無立錐。 害五也。 家人中鹽，虛占引數，轉而售人，倍支鉅萬，壞國家法，豪奪商利。 害六也。 奏求塌房，邀接商旅，倚勢賒買，恃強不償，行賈坐敝，莫敢誰何。 害七也。 賣放軍匠，名為伴當，俾辦月錢，致內府監局營作乏人，工役煩重，並力不足。 害八也。 家人貿置物料，所司畏懼，以一科十，虧官損民。 害九也。 監作所至，非法酷刑，軍匠塗炭，不勝怨酷。 害十也。 章下禮部，寢不行。
In recent years palace eunuchs Yuan Qi, Tang Shou, Xining, and Wang Zhen monopolized power and harmed government, causing state affairs to lean toward peril. I hope Your Majesty will guard against the subtle and stop the gradual, gather the reins of power, and be a model for ten thousand generations of descendants. Otherwise I fear disaster will ripen within the palace walls—the harm of Cao Jie and Hou Lan will again appear today. Your subject, though base and lowly, cannot bear it and weeps bitterly with streaming tears. I respectfully take ten matters of abusing the army and harming the people and speak of them to Your Majesty with piercing earnestness. Palace eunuchs' households accumulate gold, silver, pearls, and jade—rooms piled full, boxes overflowing—whence does it come? If not stealing from the inner treasury stores, then outwardly draining the people's fat. Harm—first. Relying on power and flaunting favor, occupying the mansions of dukes and marquises, undertaking construction corvée, toiling and harassing army and people. Harm—second. Household members and external kin are all sons of the marketplace without registration—running rampant bold and fierce, doing evil at will, contributing grain to supplement office—noble and base confused and mixed. Harm—third. Building Buddhist temples, expense beyond reckoning—serving one's private interest, ruining the property of ten thousand households. Harm—fourth. Broadly establishing estate fields, not entering tax rolls, registering households in prefectures and counties, not accepting levies and corvée—field paths stretch unbroken, while the people have no place to stand an awl. Harm—fifth. Household members obtain salt licenses, falsely occupy quota numbers, then resell to others, profiting tens of thousands in multiples—destroying state law, forcibly seizing merchants' profit. Harm—sixth. Memorializing to request warehouse sheds, inviting and receiving traveling merchants, relying on power to buy on credit, trusting in force not to repay—traveling peddlers sit ruined, none dare hold them accountable. Harm—seventh. Selling off military artisans, called companions-in-service, making them provide monthly payments—causing inner-palace supervisory offices to lack workers, labor corvée heavy and troublesome, combined strength insufficient. Harm—eighth. Household members trade and procure materials; the responsible offices fear them—one item levied as ten, harming the state and injuring the people. Harm—ninth. Wherever they supervise construction, illegal cruel punishments—military artisans in fire and charcoal, unable to bear resentment and cruelty. Harm—tenth. The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Rites; it was shelved and not implemented.
50
又有賈斌者，商河人，山西都司令史也。 亦疏言宦官之害，引漢桓帝、唐文宗、宋徽欽為戒。 且獻所輯《忠義集》四卷，采史傳所記直諫盡忠守節之士，而宦官恃寵蠹政，可為鑒戒者附焉，乞命工刊布。 禮部以其言當，乞垂鑒納，不必刊行。 帝報聞。
There was also Jia Bin, who came from Shanghe, a clerk of the Shanxi Regional Military Commission. He also submitted a memorial on the harm of palace eunuchs, citing Emperor Huan of Han, Emperor Wenzong of Tang, and Emperors Huizong and Qinzong of Song as warnings. Moreover he presented his compiled Collection of Loyal Righteousness in four volumes, gathering from histories and biographies those who directly remonstrated, exhausted loyalty, and upheld integrity—and attaching those palace eunuchs who relied on favor and corrupted government as examples for warning, begging that craftsmen be ordered to print and distribute it. The Ministry of Rites considered his words appropriate, begging that the Emperor look down and accept them—printing and distribution was not necessary. The Emperor acknowledged receipt.
51
左鼎，字周器，永新人。 正統七年進士。 明年，都御史王文以御史多闕，請會吏部於進士選補。 帝從之。 尚書王直考鼎及白圭等十餘人，曉諳刑名，皆授御史。 而鼎得南京。 尋改北，巡按山西。
Zuo Ding, styled Zhouqi, came from Yongxin. He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengtong 7. The next year, Censor-in-Chief Wang Wen, because many censor posts were vacant, asked to meet with the Ministry of Personnel to select and fill them from jinshi. The Emperor assented. Minister Wang Zhi examined Ding together with Bai Gui and more than ten others—understanding penal law—and all were appointed censors. Ding was assigned to Nanjing. Soon transferred to the north, touring and investigating Shanxi.
52
時英宗北狩，兵荒洊臻。 請蠲太原諸府稅糧，停大同轉餉夫，以蘇其困。 也先請和，抗言不可。 尋以山東、河南饑，遣鼎巡視，民賴以安。 律，官吏故勘平人致死者抵罪，時以給事中於泰言，悉得寬貰。 鼎言：「小民無知，情貸可也。 官吏深文巧詆，與故殺何異？ 法者，天下之公，不可意為輕重。 」自是論如律。
At that time Emperor Yingzong went north on hunt; war and famine arrived in succession. He asked to remit tax grain in the Taiyuan prefectures, halt Datong transport grain corvée laborers, to relieve their distress. Esen requested peace; he resisted and said it was not permissible. Soon because Shandong and Henan suffered famine, Ding was dispatched to inspect; the people relied on this for security. The law: officials who deliberately examine commoners causing death pay with their lives—at the time because Supervising Secretary Yu Tai spoke, all were broadly pardoned. Ding said: "Common people are ignorant—leniency in sentiment is acceptable. Officials who deeply twist the law and ingeniously slander—how is this different from deliberate killing? Law is the public standard of the realm under Heaven—it cannot be arbitrarily made light or heavy. " From this judgments followed the law.
53
景泰四年疏言：
In Jingtai 4 he submitted a memorial saying:
54
瓦剌變作，將士無用，由軍政不立。 謂必痛懲前弊，乃今又五年矣。 貂蟬盈座，悉屬公侯； 鞍馬塞途，莫非將帥。 民財歲耗，國帑日虛。 以天下之大，土地兵甲之眾，曾不能振揚威武，則軍政仍未立也。 昔太祖定律令，至太宗，暫許有罪者贖，蓋權宜也。 乃法吏拘牽，沿為成例，官吏受枉法財，悉得減贖。 骫骳如此，復何顧憚哉。 國初建官有常，近始因事增設。 主事每司二人，今有增至十人者矣。 御史六十人，今則百餘人矣。 甚至一部有兩尚書，侍郎亦倍常額，都御史以數十計，此京官之冗也。 外則增設撫民、管屯官。 如河南參議，益二而為四，僉事益三而為七，此外官之冗也。 天下布、按二司各十餘人，乃歲遣御史巡視，復遣大臣巡撫鎮守。 夫今之巡撫鎮守，即曩之方面御史也。 為方面御史，則合眾人之長而不足； 為巡撫鎮守，則任一人之智而有餘。 有是理邪？ 至御史遷轉太驟，當以六年為率。 令其通達政事，然後可以治人。 巡按所系尤重，毋使初任之員，漫然嘗試。 其餘百執事，皆當慎擇而久任之。 帝頗嘉納。
The Oirat rebellion erupted; generals and soldiers were useless—because military administration was not established. It was said one must severely punish previous abuses—yet now another five years have passed. Official insignia fill the seats—all are dukes and marquises; saddled horses block the roads—none are not generals and commanders. The people's wealth is exhausted yearly; the state treasury daily empties. With the realm under Heaven so vast, land and armor so numerous—yet unable to raise and display martial might—then military administration is still not established. Formerly Emperor Hongwu established laws and orders; reaching Emperor Yongle, temporarily permitting the guilty to redeem—this was expedient measure. Yet legal officials clung rigidly, following it as established precedent—officials who received unlawful bribes all could have punishment reduced through redemption. Perversity such as this—what further fear and dread is there? At the founding of the state establishing officials had constants; recently posts began to be added according to affairs. Section chiefs were two per bureau; today some have increased to ten. Censors were sixty; today there are more than a hundred. Some ministries even have two ministers; vice ministers also double the regular quota; censors-in-chief number in the tens—this is redundancy among capital officials. Externally there are added posts of pacifying-the-people and managing-garrison officials. For example Henan Administrative Commissioners increased by two to become four, Vice Commissioners increased by three to become seven—this is redundancy among external officials. Throughout the realm the provincial administration and surveillance commissions each have more than ten officials—yet yearly censors are dispatched to inspect, and again grand ministers are dispatched as grand coordinators and frontier commanders. Today's grand coordinators and frontier commanders are precisely yesterday's regional censors. As regional censors, combining everyone's strengths was insufficient; as grand coordinators and frontier commanders, entrusting one person's wisdom is more than enough. Is there such logic? As for censors, transfer is too sudden—it should take six years as the standard. Make them thoroughly understand government affairs—then they can govern people. Touring investigation bears especially heavy weight—do not let those in their first appointment casually experiment. The remaining hundred functionaries—all should be carefully selected and long appointed. The Emperor greatly praised and accepted it.
55
未幾，復言：國家承平數十年，公私之積未充。 一遇軍興，抑配橫征，鬻官市爵，率行衰世茍且之政，此司邦計者過也。 臣請痛抑末技，嚴禁遊惰，斥異端使歸南畝，裁冗員以省虛糜。 開屯田而實邊，料士伍而紓餉。 寺觀營造，供佛飯僧，以及不急之工，無益之費，悉行停罷。 專以務農重粟為本，而躬行節儉以先之，然後可阜民而裕國也。 倘忍不加務，任掊克聚斂之臣行朝三暮四之術，民力已盡而征發無已，民財已竭而賦斂日增。 茍紓目前之急，不恤意外之虞，臣竊懼焉。 章下戶部。 尚書金濂請解職，帝不許。 鼎言亦不盡行。
Before long, he again spoke: the state has enjoyed peace for several decades, yet public and private accumulations are not full. Once military campaigns arise, forced allocation and arbitrary levies, selling offices and trading noble titles—generally implementing the perfunctory policies of a declining age—this is the fault of those who manage state finance. Your subject asks to severely suppress secondary crafts, strictly forbid wandering and idleness, expel heterodox teachings making them return to southern fields, and cut redundant posts to save empty waste. Open garrison farming to solidify the frontier, assess military ranks to ease provisions. Temple and monastery construction, supplying Buddha and feeding monks, as well as non-urgent labor and useless expenses—all should be halted. Devote solely to farming and esteeming grain as foundation, and personally practice frugality to lead it—then one can enrich the people and expand the state. If one bears not to add effort, entrusting extortionate and accumulative ministers to practice morning-three-evening-four tactics—the people's strength already exhausted yet levies without end, the people's wealth already depleted yet taxes daily increase. If one merely relieves the present urgency without caring for unexpected worry, your subject secretly fears. The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Revenue. Minister Jin Lian requested to resign from office; the Emperor did not permit it. Ding's words also were not fully implemented.
56
逾月，以災異，偕同官陳救弊恤民七事。 末言：「大臣不乏奸回，宜黜罷其尤，用清政本。 」帝善其言，下詔甄別，而大臣辭職並慰留。 給事中林聰請明諭鼎等指實劾奏，鼎、聰等乃共論吏部尚書何文淵、刑部尚書俞士悅、工部侍郎張敏、通政使李錫不職狀。 錫罷，文淵致仕。
After a month, because of calamities and portents, together with colleagues he submitted seven matters of saving abuses and comforting the people. At the end he said: "Grand ministers are not lacking in treacherous and perverse men—it is fit to dismiss and remove the worst, to clarify the root of government. " The Emperor approved his words, issued an edict to distinguish and select, while grand ministers who resigned were all comforted and retained. Supervising Secretary Lin Cong asked that Ding and others be clearly instructed to impeach with concrete facts; Ding, Cong, and others then jointly discussed the incompetence of Minister of Personnel He Wenyuan, Minister of Justice Yu Shiyue, Vice Minister of Works Zhang Min, and Chief Envoy Li Xi. Xi was dismissed; Wenyuan retired.
57
鼎居官清勤，卓有聲譽。 御史練綱以敢言名，而鼎尤善為章奏。 京師語曰：「左鼎手，練綱口。 」自公卿以下咸憚之。
Ding in office was incorrupt and diligent, outstanding in reputation. Censor Lian Gang was famed for daring speech, while Ding was especially skilled at memorials. Capital saying: "Zuo Ding's hand, Lian Gang's mouth. " From dukes and ministers downward all feared them.
58
鼎出為廣東右參政。 會英宗復位，以郭登言，召為左僉都御史。 逾年卒。
Ding went out as Right Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong. When Emperor Yingzong restored the throne, on Guo Deng's recommendation he was summoned as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief. After a year he died.
59
練綱，字從道，長洲人。 祖則成，洪武時御史。 綱舉鄉試，入國子監。 歷事都察院。 郕王監國，上中興八策。 也先將入犯，復言：「和議不可就，南遷不可從，有持此議者，宜立誅。 安危所倚，惟于謙、石亨當主中軍，而分遣大臣守九門，擇親王忠孝著聞者，令同守臣勤王。 檄陜西守將調番兵入衛。 」帝悉從之。
Lian Gang, styled Congdao, came from Changzhou. His grandfather Ze Cheng was a censor in the Hongwu era. Gang passed the provincial examination and entered the National University. He served in the Censorate. When the Prince of Cheng supervised the state, he submitted eight strategies for restoration. When Esen was about to invade, he again said: "Peace talks cannot be concluded, southern relocation cannot be followed—whoever holds this view should be immediately executed. On whom safety and peril depend—only Yu Qian and Shi Heng should command the central army; grand ministers should be separately dispatched to guard the nine gates; select princes famed for loyalty and filial piety, order them together with defending officials to rescue the throne. Issue orders to Shaanxi frontier generals to transfer tribal troops to enter and guard. " The Emperor fully followed all of it.
60
綱有才辨，急功名。 都御史陳鎰、尚書俞士悅皆綱同里，念綱數陳是政有聲，且畏其口，遂薦之，授御史。
Gang had talent and eloquence, eager for fame and achievement. Censor-in-Chief Chen Yi and Minister Yu Shiyue were both Gang's fellow townsman—mindful that Gang repeatedly submitted correct policies with reputation, and also fearing his mouth, they recommended him and he was appointed censor.
61
景泰改元，上時政五事。 巡視兩淮鹽政。 駙馬都尉趙輝侵利，劾奏之。 三年冬，偕同官應詔陳八事，並允行。 亡何，復偕同官上言：「吏部推選不公，任情高下，請置尚書何文淵、右侍郎項文曜於理。 尚書王直、左侍郎俞山素行本端，為文曜等所罔，均宜按問。 」帝雖不罪，終以綱等為直。 明年命出贊延綏軍務，自陳名輕責重，乞授僉都御史。 帝曰：「遷官可自求耶？ 」遂寢其命。
When Jingtai changed the reign era, he submitted five matters on current government. He inspected the salt administration of the Two Huai. Chief Commandant of the Empress's Horse Zhao Hui encroached on profit; he impeached and memorialized him. In the winter of the third year, together with colleagues he responded to an edict and submitted eight matters—all were approved and implemented. Before long, again together with colleagues he submitted: "The Ministry of Personnel's selections are unfair, arbitrarily high or low—I ask that Minister He Wenyuan and Right Vice Minister Xiang Wenyao be brought to justice. Minister Wang Zhi and Left Vice Minister Yu Shan's conduct has always been upright, yet they were misled by Wenyao and others—all should be investigated. " Though the Emperor did not punish them, he ultimately considered Gang and others to be upright. The next year he was ordered out to assist Yan-sui military affairs; he stated himself that his name was light and responsibility heavy, begging appointment as Vice Censor-in-Chief. The Emperor said: "Can one seek promotion for oneself? " His order was thereupon shelved.
62
初，京師戒嚴，募四方民壯分營訓練，歲久多逃，或赴操不如期，廷議編之尺籍。 綱等言：「召募之初，激以忠義，許事定罷遣。 今展轉輪操，已孤所望，況其逃亡，實迫寒餒，豈可遽著軍籍。 邊方多故，倘更召募，誰復應之？ 」詔即除前令。
Initially when the capital was under martial law, sturdy men from all directions were recruited and divided into camps for training; after years many fled, or failed to report for drill on schedule—the court deliberated registering them in military rolls. Gang and others said: "At the start of recruitment, they were roused with loyalty and righteousness, promised dismissal when affairs were settled. Today rotating drill in succession has already betrayed their hopes; moreover their flight is truly forced by cold and hunger—how can they suddenly be entered in military registers. The frontier has many troubles—if recruitment is attempted again, who will respond? " An edict immediately abolished the previous order.
63
五年巡按福建，與按察使楊玨互訐，俱下吏。 謫玨黃州知府，綱邠州判官。 久之卒。
In the fifth year touring and investigating Fujian, he and Surveillance Commissioner Yang Jue mutually impeached each other—both were sent to officials for trial. Jue was demoted to Prefect of Huangzhou; Gang to Assistant Magistrate of Binzhou. After a long time he died.
64
曹凱，字宗元，益都人。 正統十年進士。 授刑科給事中。 磊落多壯節。
Cao Kai, styled Zongyuan, came from Yidu. He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengtong 10. He was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Penal Section. Open and bold, with many stalwart principles.
65
英宗北征，諫甚力，且曰：「今日之勢，大異澶淵。 彼文武忠勇，士馬勁悍。 今中貴竊權，人心玩愒。 此輩不惟以陛下為孤註，即懷、湣、徽、欽亦何暇恤？ 」帝不從，乘輿果陷。 凱痛哭竟日，聲徹禁庭，與王竑共擊馬順至死。
When Emperor Yingzong campaigned north, he remonstrated with great force, saying: "Today's situation greatly differs from Chanyuan. There civil and military were loyal and brave, troops and horses strong and fierce. Today palace favorites steal power; people's hearts are lax and weary. These men not only treat Your Majesty as a lone wager—even Emperors Huai, Min, Hui, and Qin, what leisure had they to care? " The Emperor did not follow; the imperial carriage indeed fell into peril. Kai wept bitterly all day, his voice penetrating the forbidden court; together with Wang Hong he beat Ma Shun to death.
66
景泰中，遷左。 給事中林聰劾何文淵、周旋，詔宥之。 凱上殿力諍，二人遂下吏。 時令輸豆得補官，凱爭曰：「近例，輸豆四千石以上，授指揮。 彼受祿十餘年，費已償矣，乃令之世襲，是以生民膏血養無功子孫，而彼取息長無窮也。 有功者必相謂曰：吾以捐軀獲此，彼以輸豆亦獲此，是朝廷以我軀命等於荏菽，其誰不解體！ 乞自今惟令帶俸，不得任事傳襲，文職則止原籍帶俸。 」帝以為然，命已授者如故，未授者悉如凱議。
In the Jingtai era, he was transferred to the Left Section. Supervising Secretary Lin Cong impeached He Wenyuan and Zhou Xuan; an edict pardoned them. Kai entered the hall and forcefully remonstrated; the two were thereupon sent to officials. At the time it was ordered that contributing beans could supplement office; Kai disputed, saying: "Recent precedent: contributing four thousand shi of beans or more grants commandership. They received salary for more than ten years—the cost is already repaid—yet they are allowed hereditary succession; thus the people's fat and blood nourish meritless descendants, while they draw interest endlessly. Those with achievement will surely say to each other: I obtained this by giving my body, he obtained this by contributing beans—the court equates my life with beans and millet; who will not lose heart! I beg from now only allow them to draw salary, not hold office or transmit inheritance; for civil posts, only draw salary at original domicile. " The Emperor considered it correct, ordering those already granted to remain as before, those not yet granted all according to Kai's proposal.
67
福建巡按許仕達與侍郎薛希璉相訐，命凱往勘。 用薦，擢浙江右參政。 時諸衛武職役軍辦納月錢，至四千五百餘人，以凱言禁止。 鎮守都督李信擅募民為軍，糜餉萬餘石，凱劾奏之。 信雖獲宥，諸助信募軍者咸獲罪，在浙數年，聲甚著。
Fujian touring investigator Xu Shida and Vice Minister Xue Xilian mutually impeached each other; Kai was ordered to go investigate. On recommendation, he was promoted to Right Administrative Commissioner of Zhejiang. At the time military officers of various guards forced soldiers to provide monthly payments—more than four thousand five hundred men—prohibited on Kai's word. Frontier Commander Li Xin arbitrarily recruited commoners as soldiers, wasting more than ten thousand shi of provisions; Kai impeached and memorialized him. Though Xin obtained pardon, all who helped Xin recruit soldiers were punished; serving in Zhejiang several years, his reputation was very prominent.
68
初，凱為給事，常劾武清侯石亨。 亨得志，修前憾，謫凱衛經歷，卒。
Initially when Kai was supervising secretary, he often impeached Marquis of Wuqing Shi Heng. When Heng got his wish, he settled old grudges, demoting Kai to guard intendant—he died.
69
許仕達，歙人。 正統十年進士。 擢御史。 景泰元年四月上疏言災沴數見，請帝痛自修省。 帝深納之。 未幾，復請於經筵之余，日延儒臣講論經史。 帝亦優詔褒答。 巡按福建，劾鎮守中官廖秀，下之獄。 秀訐仕達，下鎮守侍郎薛希璉等廉問。 會仕達亦劾希璉貪縱，乃命凱及御史王豪往勘。 還奏，兩人互有虛實。 而耆老數千人乞留仕達，給事中林聰，閩人也，亦為仕達言。 乃命留任，且敕希璉勿構郤。 仕達厲風紀，執漳州知府馬嗣宗送京師。 大理寺劾其擅執，帝以執贓吏不問。 期滿當代，耆老詣闕請留，不許。 未幾，即以為福建左參政。 天順中，歷山東、貴州左、右布政使。
Xu Shida came from She. He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengtong 10. He was promoted to censor. In the fourth month of Jingtai 1 he submitted a memorial saying calamities and portents appeared repeatedly, asking the Emperor to deeply examine and reform himself. The Emperor deeply accepted it. Before long, he again asked that beyond the classics lectures, scholar-officials be daily invited to discuss the Classics and histories. The Emperor also replied with a gracious edict of praise. Touring and investigating Fujian, he impeached the frontier eunuch Liao Xiu and sent him to prison. Xiu impeached Shida; frontier Vice Minister Xue Xilian and others were sent to investigate integrity. It happened that Shida also impeached Xilian for greed and indulgence; Kai and Censor Wang Hao were ordered to investigate. Returning to report, both men had truth and falsehood in their mutual accusations. Yet several thousand elders begged to retain Shida; Supervising Secretary Lin Cong, a man of Fujian, also spoke for Shida. He was ordered to remain in office, and Xilian was admonished not to create enmity. Shida enforced discipline, arrested Zhangzhou Prefect Ma Sizong and sent him to the capital. The Court of Judicial Review impeached him for unauthorized arrest; the Emperor did not inquire because he had arrested a corrupt official. When his term expired and replacement was due, elders came to the palace gates begging to retain him—not permitted. Before long he was appointed Left Administrative Commissioner of Fujian. In the Tianshun era, he served as Left and Right Provincial Administrator of Shandong and Guizhou.
70
劉煒，字有融，慈溪人。 正統四年進士。 授南京刑科給事中。 副都御史周銓以私憾撻御史。 諸御史範霖、楊永與尚褫等十人共劾銓，煒與同官盧祥等復劾之。 銓下詔獄，亦訐霖、永及煒、祥等。 王振素惡言官，盡逮下詔獄。 霖、永坐絞，後減死。 他御史或戍或謫。 煒、祥事白留任，而銓已先瘐死。 煒累進都給事中。
Liu Wei, styled Yourong, came from Cixi. He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengtong 4. He was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Penal Section at Nanjing. Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhou Quan flogged a censor out of private resentment. Censors Fan Lin, Yang Yong, and Shang Chi and nine others jointly impeached Quan; Wei together with colleagues Lu Xiang and others again impeached him. Quan was sent to the imperial prison; he also impeached Lin, Yong, Wei, Xiang, and others. Wang Zhen always hated remonstrating officials—all were arrested and sent to the imperial prison. Lin and Yong were sentenced to strangulation, later commuted from death. Other censors were either banished to garrison or demoted. Wei's and Xiang's cases were cleared and they remained in office, but Quan had already died of illness in prison. Wei was promoted in succession to Chief Supervising Secretary.
71
景泰四年，戶部以邊儲不足，奏令罷退官非贓罪者，輸米二十石，給之誥敕。 煒等言：「考退之官，多有罷軟酷虐、荒溺酒色、廉恥不立者，非止贓罪已也。 賜之誥敕，以何為辭？ 若但褒其納米，則是朝廷誥敕止直米二十石，何以示天下後世？ 此由尚書金濂不識大體，有此謬舉。 」帝立為已之。 山東歲歉，戶部以尚書沈翼習其地民瘼，請令往振。 及往，初無方略。 煒因劾翼，且言：「其地已有尚書薛希璉、少卿張固鎮撫，又有侍郎鄒幹、都御史王竑振濟，而復益之以冀，所謂『十羊九牧』。 乞還冀南京戶部，而專以命希璉等。 」從之。 平江侯陳豫鎮臨清，事多違制。 煒劾之，豫被責讓。
In Jingtai 4, because frontier stores were insufficient, the Ministry of Revenue memorialized that dismissed officials without corruption charges who contributed twenty shi of rice be granted patent of appointment. Wei and others said: "Among dismissed officials, many are weak, cruel, dissolute in wine and women, without established integrity—not only corruption charges. Granting them patents of appointment—with what words? If only praising their rice contribution, then the court's patent is worth only twenty shi of rice—how can this be shown to the realm and posterity? This is because Minister Jin Lian did not understand the larger pattern, making this absurd proposal. " The Emperor immediately stopped it. Shandong had a poor harvest; the Ministry of Revenue, because Minister Shen Yi was familiar with the people's afflictions there, asked that he be sent to provide relief. When he went, at first he had no strategy. Wei thereupon impeached Yi, saying: "That region already has Minister Xue Xilian and Junior Minister Zhang Gu pacifying, also Vice Minister Zou Gan and Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong providing relief—yet Yi is added again, what is called 'ten sheep, nine shepherds.' I beg return Yi to the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, and entrust affairs solely to Xilian and others. " It was followed. Marquis of Pingjiang Chen Yu commanded at Linqing; many affairs violated regulations. Wei impeached him; Yu was rebuked.
72
明年，都督黃竑以易儲議得帝眷，奏求霸州、武清縣地。 煒等抗章言：「竑本蠻僚，遽蒙重任。 怙寵妄幹，乞地六七十里，豈盡無主者？ 請正其罪。 」帝宥竑，遣戶部主事黃岡、謝昶往勘。 還奏，果民產。 戶部再請罪竑，帝卒宥焉。 昶官至貴州巡撫，以清慎稱。
The next year, Regional Commander Huang Gong, having gained the Emperor's favor through the heir-change debate, memorialized requesting land in Bazhou and Wuqing counties. Wei and others submitted a resisting memorial saying: "Gong is originally a tribal frontier officer, suddenly receiving heavy appointment. Relying on favor he recklessly interferes, begging for land sixty or seventy li—are there none with owners? I ask that his crime be corrected. " The Emperor pardoned Gong, sending Ministry of Revenue Section Chiefs Huang Gang and Xie Chang to investigate. Returning to report, it was indeed people's property. The Ministry of Revenue again asked to punish Gong; the Emperor ultimately pardoned him. Chang rose to Grand Coordinator of Guizhou, famed for integrity and caution.
73
煒天順初出為雲南參政，改廣東，分守惠、潮二府。 潮有巨寇，招之不服，會兵進剿，誅其魁。 改蒞南韶。 會大軍征兩廣，以勞瘁卒官。
At the start of Tianshun Wei went out as Administrative Commissioner of Yunnan, transferred to Guangdong, separately guarding Huizhou and Chaozhou prefectures. Chaozhou had a great bandit; summoned he would not submit—gathering troops they advanced to suppress and executed the leader. He was transferred to oversee Nanxun. When the great army campaigned in the Two Guangs, he died in office from exhaustion.
74
尚褫，字景福，羅山人。 正統四年進士。 除行人。 上書請毋囚系大臣。 擢南御史。 以劾周銓下獄，與他御史皆謫驛丞，得雲南虛仁驛。 景泰五年冬因災異上書陳數事，中言：「忠直之士，冒死陳言。 執政者格以條例，輕則報罷，重則中傷，是言路雖開猶未開也。 釋教盛行，誘煽聾俗，由掌邦禮者畏王振勢，度僧多至此，宜盡勒歸農。 」章下禮部，尚書胡濙惡其刺己，悉格不行。 量移豐城知縣，為邑豪誣構系獄，尋得釋。
Shang Chi, styled Jingfu, came from Luoshan. He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengtong 4. He was appointed Courier. He submitted a memorial asking that grand ministers not be imprisoned. He was promoted to Nanjing censor. For impeaching Zhou Quan he was imprisoned; together with other censors all were demoted to post station assistants—he obtained Xuren Post in Yunnan. In the winter of Jingtai 5, because of calamities and portents he submitted a memorial on several matters, saying among other things: "Loyal and upright men risk death to speak. Those in power block them with regulations—lightly they are dismissed with a reply, heavily they are slandered—thus though the path of speech is open, it is still not open. Buddhism flourishes, seducing and inciting the deafened masses—because those who manage state rites fear Wang Zhen's power, ordained monks are many to this point—it is fit to compel them all to return to farming. " The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Rites; Minister Hu Ying hated that it stabbed at him—all was blocked and not implemented. He was transferred laterally to magistrate of Fengcheng; framed by local bullies and imprisoned, soon released.
75
成化初，大臣會薦，擢湖廣僉事。 初有詔，荊、襄流民，許所在附籍。 都御史項忠復遣還鄉，督其急，多道死。 褫憫之，陳牒巡撫吳琛請進止。 琛以報忠，忠怒劾褫。 中朝知其意在恤民，卒申令流民聽附籍，不願，乃遣還鄉。 褫為僉事十年，所司上其治行，賜誥旌異。 致仕卒。
At the start of Chenghua, grand ministers jointly recommended him; he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Huguang. Initially there was an edict: Jing and Xiang displaced persons were permitted to register wherever they were. Censor-in-Chief Xiang Zhong again sent them back to their villages, pressing them urgently—many died on the roads. Chi pitied them, submitted a document to Grand Coordinator Wu Chen asking for advance or halt. Chen reported to Zhong; Zhong angrily impeached Chi. The court knew his intent was to comfort the people; ultimately the order was reissued that displaced persons might register if willing—if unwilling, then send back to villages. Chi served as vice commissioner ten years; his supervising office reported his governing conduct; he was granted patent and specially commended. He retired and died.
76
單宇。 字時泰，臨川人。 正統四年進士。 除嵊縣知縣。 馭吏嚴。 吏欲誣奏宇，宇以聞。 坐不並上吏奏，逮下獄。 事白，調諸暨。
Dan Yu. Styled Shitai, came from Linchuan. He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengtong 4. He was appointed magistrate of Sheng County. He controlled clerks strictly. Clerks wished to frame and memorialize Yu; Yu reported it. Convicted for not jointly submitting the clerks' memorial, he was arrested and imprisoned. The case cleared; he was transferred to Zhuji.
77
遭喪服除，待銓京師。 適英宗北狩，宇憤中官監軍，諸將不得專進止，致喪師。 疏請盡罷之，以重將權。 景帝不納。
After mourning and removal of mourning garments, he awaited appointment selection in the capital. It happened that Emperor Yingzong went north on hunt; Yu was indignant that palace eunuchs supervised the army, generals could not exclusively advance or halt, causing loss of the army. He memorialized asking that they all be abolished, to emphasize generals' authority. Emperor Jingtai did not accept it.
78
