初，王振佞佛，請帝歲一度僧。 其所修大興隆寺，日役萬人，糜帑數十萬，閎麗冠京都。 英宗為賜號「第一叢林」，命僧大作佛事，躬自臨幸，以故釋教益熾。 至是宇上書言：「前代人君尊奉佛氏，卒致禍亂。 近男女出家累百千萬，不耕不織，蠶食民間。 營構寺宇，遍滿京邑，所費不可勝紀。 請撤木石以建軍營，銷銅鐵以鑄兵仗，罷遣僧尼，歸之民俗，庶皇風清穆，異教不行。 」疏入，為廷議所格。 復知侯官。
Initially Wang Zhen flattered Buddhism, asking the Emperor to ordain monks once a year. The Great Xinglong Temple he built daily employed ten thousand men, wasted hundreds of thousands from the treasury—grand and splendid, foremost in the capital. Emperor Yingzong granted it the title "First Monastic Grove," ordered monks to perform great Buddhist rites, personally visited—thus Buddhism grew more fervent. At this Yu submitted a memorial saying: "Former ages' rulers honored and served the Buddha, ultimately bringing disaster and disorder. Recently men and women leaving home number cumulatively millions—neither plowing nor weaving, silkworm-eating the common people. Constructing temples and monasteries, filling the capital region—the expense cannot be fully recorded. I ask to dismantle wood and stone to build military camps, melt copper and iron to cast weapons, dismiss monks and nuns and return them to common custom—then perhaps imperial wind will be clear and solemn, heterodox teachings will not prevail. " The memorial entered; it was blocked by court deliberation. He was again appointed magistrate of Houguan.
79
而咸陽姚顯以鄉舉入國學，亦上言：「曩者修治大興隆寺，窮極壯麗，又奉僧楊某為上師，儀從侔王者。 食膏粱，被組繡，藐萬乘若弟子。 今上皇被留賊庭，乞令前赴瓦剌，化諭也先。 誠能奉駕南還，庶見護國之力。 不然，佛不足信彰彰矣。 」當景泰時，廷臣諫事佛者甚眾，帝卒不能從。 而中官興安最用事，佞佛甚於振。 請帝建大隆福寺，嚴壯與興隆並。 四年三月，寺成，帝克期臨幸。 河東鹽運判官濟寧楊浩切諫，乃止。
Meanwhile Yao Xian of Xianyang entered the National University through provincial recommendation, also submitting: "Formerly in repairing the Great Xinglong Temple, extravagance reached the utmost; moreover a monk surnamed Yang was honored as supreme teacher, his retinue equaling a king's. Eating fine grain, wearing brocade, treating the Son of Heaven lightly as a disciple. Today the Retired Emperor is detained in the bandits' court—I beg order him forward to the Oirat, to convert and instruct Esen. If truly he can escort the carriage south in return, then perhaps the power of protecting the state will be seen. Otherwise, that the Buddha is not worth trusting is abundantly clear. " In the Jingtai era, court ministers remonstrating about Buddhist affairs were very many—the Emperor ultimately could not follow them. Yet palace eunuch Xing An was most in power, flattering Buddhism even more than Zhen. He asked the Emperor to build the Great Longfu Temple, solemn and grand, equal to Xinglong. In the third month of the fourth year the temple was complete; the Emperor set a date to visit. Hedong Salt Transport Assistant Magistrate Yang Hao of Jining remonstrated sharply—it was then stopped.
80
宇好學有文名，三為縣，咸以慈惠聞。 居侯官，久之卒。
Yu loved learning and had a literary reputation; thrice serving as magistrate, all were known for kindness and grace. Serving at Houguan, after a long time he died.
81
顯後為齊東知縣，移武城，公廉剛正。 用巡撫翁世資薦，擢太僕丞。 浩初以鄉舉入國學，除官未行，遂抗疏，聲譽籍甚。 累官右副都御史，巡撫延綏。
Xian later served as magistrate of Qidong, transferred to Wucheng—public-spirited, incorrupt, stern and upright. On Grand Coordinator Weng Shizi's recommendation, he was promoted to Assistant Director of the Imperial Stud. Hao initially entered the National University through provincial recommendation; before taking office he submitted a resisting memorial—his reputation was very great. Rising in office to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, Grand Coordinator of Yan-sui.
82
張昭，不知何許人。 天順初，為忠義前衛吏。 英宗復辟甫數月，欲遣都指揮馬雲等使西洋，廷臣莫敢諫。 昭聞之，上疏曰：「安內救民，國家之急務，慕外勤遠，朝廷之末策。 漢光武閉關謝西域，唐太宗不受康國內附，皆深知本計者也。 今畿輔、山東仍歲災歉，小民絕食逃竄，妻子衣不蔽體，被薦裹席，鬻子女無售者。 家室不相完，轉死溝壑，未及埋瘞，已成市臠，此可為痛哭者也。 望陛下用和番之費，益以府庫之財，急遣使振恤，庶饑民可救。 」奏下公卿博議，言雲等已罷遣。 宜籍記所市物俟命。 帝命姑已之。
Zhang Zhao—of unknown origin. At the start of Tianshun, he was a clerk of the Loyal Righteous Forward Guard. Emperor Yingzong had restored the throne only a few months when he wished to dispatch Chief Commandant Ma Yun and others as envoys to the Western Ocean—court ministers none dared remonstrate. Zhao heard of it and submitted a memorial saying: "Pacifying within and saving the people is the state's urgent task; admiring the outer and toiling for the distant is the court's last resort. Han Guangwu closed the passes and declined the Western Regions; Tang Taizong did not accept Kang's submission—all deeply knew the fundamental plan. Today the capital region and Shandong suffer disaster and poor harvest year after year—common people lack food and flee, wives and children with clothes not covering their bodies, wrapped in straw mats, selling sons and daughters with no buyers. Households not preserved whole, turning to die in ditches and gullies—before burial, already become market meat—this is cause for bitter weeping. I hope Your Majesty will use the expense for pacifying the frontier tribes, add treasury wealth, urgently dispatch envoys to provide relief—then perhaps starving people can be saved. " The memorial was sent down for broad deliberation among dukes and ministers—they said Yun and others had already been dismissed and sent away. It is fit to register and record purchased goods awaiting orders. The Emperor ordered it temporarily stopped.
83
天順三年秋，建安老人賀煬亦上書論時事，言：「今銓授縣令，多年老監生。 逮滿九載，年幾七十，茍且貪汙。 宜擇年富有才能者，其下僚及山林抱德士，亦當推舉。 景泰朝，錄先賢顏、孟、程、朱子孫，授以翰林博士，俾之奉祀。 然有官無祿，宜班給以昭崇儒之意。 黃幹、劉爚、蔡沈、真德秀配祠朱子，亦景泰間從僉事呂昌之請，然未入祝辭，宜增補。 預備義倉，本以振貧民，乃豪猾多冒支不償，致廩庾空虛。 乞令出粟義民，各疏裏內饑民，同有司散放。 」未幾，又言：「朝廷建學立師，將以陶熔士類。 而師儒鮮積學，草野小夫夤緣津要，初解免園之冊，已廁鶚薦之群。 及受職泮林，猥瑣貪饕，要求百故； 而授業解惑，莫措一詞。 生徒亦往往玩愒歲月，佻達城闕，待次循資，濫升太學，侵尋老耋，幸博一官。 但廑身家之謀，無復功名之念。 及今不嚴甄選，人材日陋。 士習日非矣。 」帝善其言，下所司行之。
In the autumn of Tianshun 3, the old man He Yang of Jian'an also submitted a memorial on current affairs, saying: "Today in selecting and appointing county magistrates, many are elderly supervising students. When nine years are complete, age nearly seventy—they are perfunctory and corrupt. It is fit to select those rich in years and ability; subordinate officials and reclusive men of virtue in mountains and forests should also be recommended. In the Jingtai court, descendants of former sages Yan, Meng, Cheng, and Zhu were recorded, granted Hanlin Erudite posts, made to perform sacrifices. Yet they have office without salary—it is fit to grant stipends in rotation to display the intent of honoring Confucianism. Huang Gan, Liu Yan, Cai Shen, and Zhen Dexiu were enshrined with Zhu Xi—also in Jingtai on Vice Commissioner Lü Chang's request—yet not entered in sacrificial prayers; it is fit to add and supplement. Prepared charity granaries were originally to relieve the poor—yet powerful rascals often falsely drew without repayment, causing granaries to stand empty. I beg order grain-contributing public-spirited commoners each to list hungry people within their neighborhood, together with local officials to distribute. " Before long, again he said: "The court establishes schools and appoints teachers, intending to mold and fuse the scholar class. Yet teachers and scholars rarely accumulate learning; petty men of the wilds cling to critical posts—just having finished the Mianyuan primer, already placed among the recommended flock. When receiving office in the academy grove, they are petty and greedy, demanding every sort of thing; yet in teaching and resolving doubts, they cannot manage a single phrase. Students also often waste years in idleness, frivolous at the capital gates, awaiting turn by seniority, indiscriminately rising to the National University, gradually reaching old age, lucky to win one office. They care only for schemes of personal wealth, no longer thoughts of fame and achievement. If now selection is not strictly applied, talent daily grows coarse. Scholars' habits daily decline. " The Emperor approved his words and sent them down to responsible offices for implementation.
84
高瑤，字庭堅，閩縣人。 由鄉舉為荊門州學訓導。 成化三年五月抗疏陳十事。 其一言：「正統己巳之變，先帝北狩，陛下方在東宮，宗社危如一發。 使非郕王繼統，國有長君，則禍亂何由平、鑒輿何由返？ 六七年間，海宇寧謐，元元樂業，厥功不細。 迨先帝復辟，貪天功者遂加厚誣，使不得正其終，節惠隮祀，未稱典禮。 望特敕禮官集議，追加廟號，盡親親之恩。 」章下，廷議久不決。 至十二月始奏：「追崇廟號，非臣下敢擅議，惟陛下裁決。 」而左庶子黎淳力爭，謂不當復，且言：「瑤此言有死罪二：一誣先帝為不明，一陷陛下於不孝。 臣以謂瑤此舉，非欲尊郕王，特為群邪進用階，必有小人主之者。 」帝曰：「景泰往過，朕未嘗介意，豈臣子所當言？ 淳為此奏，欲獻諂希恩耶？ 」議遂寢。 然帝終感瑤言。 久之，竟復郕王帝號。
Gao Yao, styled Tingjian, came from Min County. Through provincial recommendation he became Instructor of Jingmen Prefecture School. In the fifth month of Chenghua 3 he submitted a resisting memorial stating ten matters. The first said: "In the jisi year change of Zhengtong, the former Emperor went north on hunt, Your Majesty was still in the Eastern Palace—the altars of state perilous as a single hair. If not for the Prince of Cheng succeeding the throne, the state having a mature ruler—then how would disaster and disorder be pacified, how would the imperial carriage return? For six or seven years, sea and land were tranquil, the masses rejoiced in their work—his achievement was not small. When the former Emperor restored the throne, those who coveted heavenly achievement then added heavy slander, making him unable to end properly—honoring his integrity and ascending sacrifices did not match canonical rites. I hope Your Majesty will specially order rites officials to gather and deliberate, add posthumous temple title, exhaust the kindness of treating kin as kin. " The memorial was sent down; court deliberation long did not decide. Only in the twelfth month did they memorialize: "Posthumous temple title elevation—subordinates dare not deliberate on their own; only Your Majesty decides. " But Left Sub-Reader Li Chun forcefully disputed, saying it should not be restored, and said: "Yao's words have two capital crimes: one slandering the former Emperor as unenlightened, one trapping Your Majesty in unfiliality. Your subject considers Yao's act is not wishing to honor the Prince of Cheng—it is specially a stair for wicked groups to advance; there must be petty men directing it. " The Emperor said: "Jingtai's past faults—I have never minded them; is this what subjects should speak of? Chun makes this memorial—wishing to offer flattery and hope for favor? " Deliberation was thereupon shelved. Yet the Emperor ultimately was moved by Yao's words. After a long time, he finally restored the Prince of Cheng's imperial title.
85
瑤後知番禺縣，多異政。 發中官韋眷通番事，沒其貲鉅萬於官。 眷憾甚，誣奏於朝。 瑤及布政使陳選俱被逮，士民泣送者塞道。 瑤竟謫戍永州。 釋還，卒。
Yao later served as magistrate of Panyu, with many unusual achievements in government. He exposed palace eunuch Wei Juan's illegal trade with foreign lands, confiscating his assets of tens of thousands for the state. Juan resented deeply and falsely memorialized at court. Yao and Provincial Administrator Chen Xuan were both arrested; scholars and commoners weeping to see them off blocked the roads. Yao was ultimately demoted to garrison duty at Yongzhou. Released and returned; he died.
86
黎淳，華容人。 天順元年進士第一。 官至南京禮部尚書，頗有名譽。 其與瑤爭郕王廟號也，專欲阿憲宗意，至以昌邑、更始比景帝，為士論所薄。 當成化時，言路大阻，給事、御史多獲譴。 惟瑤以卑官建危議，卒無罪。 時皆稱帝盛德雲。
Li Chun came from Huarong. He ranked first in the jinshi examination in Tianshun 1. His office reached Minister of Rites at Nanjing, with considerable reputation. In disputing with Yao over the Prince of Cheng's temple title, he solely wished to flatter Emperor Xianzong's intent—even comparing Emperor Jingtai to Changyi and Gengshi, and was scorned by scholarly opinion. In the Chenghua era, the path of speech was greatly blocked; supervising secretaries and censors often received punishment. Only Yao, as a low official raising a perilous proposal, ultimately was not punished. At the time all praised the Emperor's great virtue.
87
又有虎臣者，麟遊人。 成化中貢入太學。 上言天下士大夫過先聖廟，宜下輿馬。 從之。 省親歸，會陜西大饑，巡撫鄭時將請振，臣賫奏行，陳饑歉狀，詞激切，大獲振貸。 已，上言：「臣鄉比歲災傷，人相食，由長吏貪殘，賦役失均。 請敕有司審民戶，編三等以定科徭。 」從之。 孝宗踐阼，將建棕棚萬歲山，備登眺。 臣抗疏切諫。 祭酒費訚懼禍及，鋃鐺縶臣堂樹下。 俄官校宣臣至左順門，傳旨慰諭曰：「若言是，棕棚已毀矣。 」訚大慚，臣名遂聞都下。 頃之，命授七品官，乃以為雲南嘉知縣，卒官。
There was also Hu Chen, who came from Linyou. In the Chenghua era he entered the National University as a tribute student. He submitted that when scholar-officials throughout the realm pass the Former Sage Temple, they should dismount from carriage and horse. It was followed. Returning home to visit kin, it happened that Shaanxi suffered great famine; Grand Coordinator Zheng Shi was about to request relief—Chen carried a memorial on his journey, stating the famine conditions, his words sharp and urgent, greatly obtaining relief grain. Afterward he submitted: "In my home district in recent years disaster and injury—people eating one another—stem from chief officials' greed and cruelty, taxes and corvée unequally apportioned. I ask order responsible offices to examine household registers, compile three grades to fix levies and corvée. " It was followed. When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, he was about to build a palm-frond pavilion on Longevity Hill for viewing from afar. Chen submitted a resisting memorial remonstrating sharply. Libationer Fei Yin feared disaster would reach him, shackled Chen with iron chains under a hall tree. Soon court runners summoned Chen to the Left Compliance Gate, transmitting an edict of comfort saying: "If your words are correct, the palm-frond pavilion has already been destroyed. " Yin was greatly ashamed; Chen's name then became known throughout the capital. Before long he was ordered granted a seventh-rank office; he was made magistrate of Jia in Yunnan and died in office.
88
贊曰：明自太祖開基，廣辟言路。 中外臣寮，建言不拘所職。 草野微賤，奏章咸得上聞。 沿及宣、英，流風未替。 雖升平日久，堂陛深嚴，而逢掖布衣。 刀筆掾史，抱關之冗吏，荷戈之戍卒，朝陳封事，夕達帝閽。 采納者榮顯其身，報罷者亦不之罪。 若仁宗之復弋謙朝參，引咎自責，即懸鞀設鐸，復何以加。 以此為招，宜乎慷慨發憤之徒扼腕而談世務也。 英、景之際，《實錄》所載，不可勝書。 今掇其著者列於篇。 迨憲宗季年，閹尹擅朝，事勢屢變，別自為卷，得有考焉。
Commentary says: Ming from Emperor Hongwu's founding broadly opened the path of speech. Internal and external ministers and officials submitted advice without binding by their duties. Humble and lowly in the wilds—all memorials could reach the Emperor's hearing. Extending through Xuanzong and Yingzong, the flowing custom was not replaced. Though long years of peace and prosperity, hall and steps deep and stern—yet scholars in wide sleeves and common cloth. Brush-and-knife clerks and runners, gate-keeping redundant officials, spear-bearing garrison soldiers—in the morning presenting sealed memorials, by evening reaching the imperial gate. Those adopted were honored and displayed in person; those dismissed with a reply were also not punished. Like Renzong restoring Yi Qian's court attendance, taking blame upon himself—even hanging drums and setting bells, what could be added? With this as invitation, it is fitting that men of generous spirit and indignant passion should clench their wrists and discuss affairs of the age. In the Ying and Jing transition, what the Veritable Records record cannot be fully written. Now I gather the prominent ones and list them in this chapter. Reaching the late years of Emperor Xianzong, eunuch chiefs monopolized the court, affairs repeatedly changed—they are separately made a volume, so there can be examination.
